import Mathlib
/-! QED-M033: Binary-error LWE with linearly many samples
For LWE with secret in Z_q^n (q = poly(n)) and uniform binary errors, given m = Cn samples for a fixed
C > 1: find a subexponential algorithm or prove hardness from standard LWE.
Informal statement: Fix q = q(n) with 2 ≤ q(n) ≤ poly(n) and a constant C > 1; let m = ⌈Cn⌉. In
decision binary-error LWE one is given (A, b) with A uniform in Z_q^{m×n} and either b = As + e mod q
(s uniform in Z_q^n, e uniform in {0,1}^m) or b uniform in Z_q^m. Show that (for every such C and q) one of
the following holds: (a) some randomized algorithm running in time 2^{o(n)} distinguishes the two cases
with non-negligible advantage; or (b) binary-error LWE with these parameters is hard (no poly-time
distinguisher has non-negligible advantage) assuming standard decision LWE is hard for some standard
parameter family (dimension n' polynomially related to n, modulus and sample count poly(n), discrete
Gaussian error of width αq' ≥ 2√n'). Known: Arora-Ge linearization solves it in poly time for m ≈ n²;
Micciancio-Peikert prove (b) for m = n(1+O(1/log n)).
Formalization notes:
* Machine model: the board's canonical word-RAM block (pasted verbatim below). A distinguisher is a
  `WRAlgo`; it accepts when it halts within the budget with output `[1]` (non-halting runs reject, so the
  budget is a worst-case clock). `wrProb` is the exact probability over a uniform random tape.
  Every statement quantifies over all word sizes admissible for every instance of the given size
  (w ≥ (wc+1)·log(input length) and all words < 2^w).
* Inputs: `[n, m, q]`, then A row-major, then b (all entries < q, one word each). Probabilities are exact
  finite averages (binary case) or weighted sums with the discrete Gaussian mass function (standard case).
* Discrete Gaussian: ρ_s(z) = exp(-π z²/s²) on ℤ, normalized by Σ_z ρ_s(z), reduced mod q' (`dgMod`);
  this is the standard D_{ℤ,s} mod q' error of Regev/Peikert LWE with s = αq'.
* Advantage `adv` = |Pr[accept | LWE] - Pr[accept | uniform]|. `Breaks T` = for some d, for infinitely many n,
  at every admissible word size the advantage with budget O(T n) is ≥ n^{-d} (non-negligible).
  Hardness = no algorithm Breaks with polynomial budget (exactly the negation, quantified over all
  algorithms and all polynomial budgets C·n^c).
* (a) = `BinEasy C q`: one algorithm with budget O(2^{f(n)}), f(n)/n → 0, breaks binary LWE.
  (b) = some standard parameter family `P` (`StdParams`: 2 ≤ q'(n) ≤ n^c, m'(n) ≤ n^c, n ≤ n'(n)^c,
  1 ≤ n'(n) ≤ n^c, width ≥ 2√n') with `LWEHard P → BinHard C q`. "Polynomial loss" is captured because
  both sides are about polynomial time and non-negligible advantage, closed under polynomial blowups.
  The implication form (rather than an explicit black-box reduction) is the standard way to state
  "as hard as LWE"; any black-box reduction proves it.
* Decision versions are used throughout: for (a) distinguishing is the weaker requirement (search ⇒
  decision), and decision-hardness is what the cryptographic applications and Micciancio–Peikert give.
* Judgement call: the informal "either (a) or (b)" is formalized as the dichotomy
  Claim := ∀ C > 1, ∀ poly-bounded q, (a) ∨ (b). Proving Claim settles every (C, q) (possibly with the
  answer depending on (C, q)); ¬Claim exhibits (C, q) where neither holds (no 2^{o(n)} attack exists and
  hardness does not follow from LWE in this sense), which would itself require an unconditional lower
  bound. Loophole audit: for q = 2 binary errors make b exactly uniform, so (a) fails and (b) holds
  (BinHard is then true outright) — correct behaviour; the constraint width ≥ 2√n' keeps the LWE
  hypothesis from being trivially refutable (tiny error ⇒ Gaussian elimination).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM033
noncomputable section

/-! ### Canonical word-RAM model (QED board, shared block; paste verbatim inside the problem namespace)

* A machine has word size `w`; every register and memory cell holds a natural number `< 2^w`
  (invariant: every register write is reduced mod `2^w`; memory only receives register values
  and input words, which are required to be `< 2^w`).
* Registers `R : ℕ → ℕ` (a program mentions only finitely many) and memory `M : ℕ → ℕ`
  (addresses are register values, hence `< 2^w`: at most `2^w` cells, all initially 0 except input).
* Program: a finite list of the standard unit-cost instructions below; `pc` indexes the list.
  A `pc` outside the list (in particular after `halt`, or a jump past the end) means halted, and a
  halted configuration is a fixed point of `wrStep`.
* Input: a list of words `x₀ … x_{n-1}` placed in `M[0..n-1]`; initially `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`,
  all other registers 0. Output: on halting, `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`.
* Randomness: instruction `rand d` reads the next word of a random tape (word `k` is
  `tape k mod 2^w`). Deterministic runs use the all-zero tape.
* Cost: one step per instruction. `RunsWithin` asks the machine to be halted after `t` steps.
* Word size: an algorithm carries a constant `wc`, and must be correct for EVERY word size
  `w ≥ (wc+1)·(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` for which all input words fit (`< 2^w`). Requiring all such `w`
  (rather than letting the algorithm pick `w`) rules out the "huge word" loophole: the time bound
  must already hold at `w = Θ(log n)`, while larger `w` never hurts (the program can mask).
-/

/-- The instruction set (all unit cost). Indices `d a b` are register names, `t` a program address. -/
inductive WRInstr where
  /-- `R d := c mod 2^w` (a fixed program constant). -/
  | const (d c : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := M[R a]` (indirect load). -/
  | load (d a : ℕ)
  /-- `M[R a] := R s` (indirect store). -/
  | store (a s : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a + R b) mod 2^w`. -/
  | add (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := R a - R b`, truncated at 0. -/
  | sub (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a * R b) mod 2^w` (low word of the product). -/
  | mul (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := ⌊R a / R b⌋` (and `x / 0 = 0`). -/
  | div (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Bitwise and / or / xor. -/
  | band (d a b : ℕ)
  | bor (d a b : ℕ)
  | bxor (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a · 2^(R b)) mod 2^w` and `R d := ⌊R a / 2^(R b)⌋`. -/
  | shl (d a b : ℕ)
  | shr (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Unconditional jump; jump if `R a = 0`; jump if `R a < R b`. -/
  | jmp (t : ℕ)
  | jz (a t : ℕ)
  | jlt (a b t : ℕ)
  /-- `R d :=` next random word. -/
  | rand (d : ℕ)
  /-- Stop. -/
  | halt

/-- Machine configuration: program counter, registers, memory, number of random words used. -/
structure WRCfg where
  pc : ℕ
  reg : ℕ → ℕ
  mem : ℕ → ℕ
  rc : ℕ

/-- One step of program `prog` with word size `w` and random tape `tape`. -/
def wrStep (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (s : WRCfg) : WRCfg :=
  match prog[s.pc]? with
  | none => s
  | some ins =>
    let upd : ℕ → ℕ → WRCfg := fun d v =>
      { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (v % 2 ^ w) }
    let jump : Bool → ℕ → WRCfg := fun b t =>
      { s with pc := if b then t else s.pc + 1 }
    match ins with
    | .const d c => upd d c
    | .load d a => upd d (s.mem (s.reg a))
    | .store a r => { s with pc := s.pc + 1, mem := Function.update s.mem (s.reg a) (s.reg r) }
    | .add d a b => upd d (s.reg a + s.reg b)
    | .sub d a b => upd d (s.reg a - s.reg b)
    | .mul d a b => upd d (s.reg a * s.reg b)
    | .div d a b => upd d (s.reg a / s.reg b)
    | .band d a b => upd d (Nat.land (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bor d a b => upd d (Nat.lor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bxor d a b => upd d (Nat.xor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .shl d a b => upd d (s.reg a * 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .shr d a b => upd d (s.reg a / 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .jmp t => { s with pc := t }
    | .jz a t => jump (decide (s.reg a = 0)) t
    | .jlt a b t => jump (decide (s.reg a < s.reg b)) t
    | .rand d =>
        { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (tape s.rc % 2 ^ w), rc := s.rc + 1 }
    | .halt => { s with pc := prog.length }

/-- Initial configuration: input in `M[0..n-1]`, `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`. -/
def wrInit (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) : WRCfg where
  pc := 0
  reg := fun i => if i = 0 then input.length else if i = 1 then w else 0
  mem := fun a => input.getD a 0
  rc := 0

/-- Output of a configuration: `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`. -/
def wrOutput (s : WRCfg) : List ℕ := (List.range (s.reg 0)).map s.mem

/-- Halted: the program counter has left the program. -/
def WRHalted (prog : List WRInstr) (s : WRCfg) : Prop := prog.length ≤ s.pc

/-- With random tape `tape`, the run on `input` has halted after `t` steps (i.e. within `t` steps,
since halted configurations are fixed points) with output `out`. -/
def RunsWithinR (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ)
    (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) ∧
    wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) = out

/-- Deterministic run (all-zero random tape). -/
def RunsWithin (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  RunsWithinR prog w (fun _ => 0) input t out

/-- An algorithm: a program and a word-size constant `wc` (it may assume `w ≥ (wc+1)·log n`). -/
structure WRAlgo where
  prog : List WRInstr
  wc : ℕ

/-- Admissible word sizes for an input: `w ≥ (wc+1)(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` (so `n < 2^w`) and every
input word fits in `w` bits. -/
def WROK (wc : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (w : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (wc + 1) * (Nat.log 2 (input.length + 1) + 1) ≤ w ∧ ∀ x ∈ input, x < 2 ^ w

/-- The step budget `⌊C·T + C⌋₊` used for "time O(T)" (the additive `C` absorbs small inputs). -/
def wrBudget (C T : ℝ) : ℕ := ⌊C * T + C⌋₊

/-- A (batch) problem: instances, a word encoding of each instance, and the set of correct outputs. -/
structure WRProblem where
  Inst : Type
  enc : Inst → List ℕ
  Correct : Inst → List ℕ → Prop

/-- Deterministic: some algorithm solves every instance `x` within `O(T x)` steps, for every
admissible word size. (`T` may depend on any parameters of the instance.) -/
def WRSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithin A.prog w (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧ P.Correct x out

/-- The random tape determined by `L` random `w`-bit words (word `k ≥ L` reads as 0; a run of `L`
steps reads at most `L` words, so uniform `f` is exactly a uniformly random tape). -/
def wrTape {L w : ℕ} (f : Fin L → Fin (2 ^ w)) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  fun k => if h : k < L then (f ⟨k, h⟩ : ℕ) else 0

/-- Randomized (Monte Carlo, worst-case time): for every instance and admissible `w`, at least 2/3
of the random tapes make the algorithm halt within `O(T x)` steps with a correct output. -/
def WRRandSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (T x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (T x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithinR A.prog w (wrTape f) (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧
          P.Correct x out}

/-! #### Online (multi-phase) variant
Phase inputs `x₀, x₁, …` arrive one at a time. Before phase `j` the words of `x_j` overwrite
`M[0..|x_j|-1]`, `R 0 := |x_j|`, `pc := 0`; all other registers, memory and the random-tape position
persist. The phase's output is read when it halts. Phase `j` cannot see `x_{j+1}`, so answers are
online. Inputs are fixed in advance (oblivious adversary). -/

/-- Feed the next phase input into a (halted) configuration. -/
def wrFeed (s : WRCfg) (x : List ℕ) : WRCfg :=
  { s with pc := 0, reg := Function.update s.reg 0 x.length,
           mem := fun a => if a < x.length then x.getD a 0 else s.mem a }

/-- `wrPhases prog w tape s xs ts os`: starting from `s`, phase `j` gets input `xs[j]`, halts within
`ts[j]` steps and outputs `os[j]`. -/
def wrPhases (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) :
    WRCfg → List (List ℕ) → List ℕ → List (List ℕ) → Prop
  | _, [], [], [] => True
  | s, x :: xs, t :: ts, o :: os =>
      WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) ∧
      wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) = o ∧
      wrPhases prog w tape ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) xs ts os
  | _, _, _, _ => False

/-- An online problem: instances, the list of phase inputs, and correct lists of phase outputs. -/
structure WROnlineProblem where
  Inst : Type
  phases : Inst → List (List ℕ)
  Correct : Inst → List (List ℕ) → Prop

/-- All words of all phases. -/
def wrAllWords (xs : List (List ℕ)) : List ℕ := xs.foldr (· ++ ·) []

/-- Randomized online solution with first-phase (preprocessing) time `O(Tpre x)` and total time of
all later phases `O(Tq x)` (so amortized time per later phase is `Tq x / (#phases - 1)`). -/
def WROnlineRandSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
          wrPhases A.prog w (wrTape f) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
          (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
          P.Correct x outs}

/-- Deterministic online solution (all-zero tape). -/
def WROnlineSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
      wrPhases A.prog w (fun _ => 0) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
      (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
      P.Correct x outs

/-! #### Encoding helpers -/

/-- Boolean as a word. -/
def wrBit (b : Bool) : ℕ := cond b 1 0

/-- Integer as a word (zig-zag: `z ≥ 0 ↦ 2z`, `z < 0 ↦ 2|z| + 1`). -/
def wrInt (z : ℤ) : ℕ := 2 * z.natAbs + (if z < 0 then 1 else 0)

/-- A list of pairs as a flat list of words. -/
def wrPairs : List (ℕ × ℕ) → List ℕ
  | [] => []
  | p :: l => p.1 :: p.2 :: wrPairs l

/-- Output `out` is the yes/no answer to `b`: `[1]` if `b`, `[0]` otherwise. -/
def WRAnswer (b : Prop) (out : List ℕ) : Prop := (b ∧ out = [1]) ∨ (¬ b ∧ out = [0])

/-- Probability over a uniform random tape of `t` words that the run on `input` halts within `t`
steps with output `out`. -/
def wrProb (prog : List WRInstr) (w t : ℕ) (input out : List ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (Nat.card {f : Fin t → Fin (2 ^ w) // RunsWithinR prog w (wrTape f) input t out} : ℝ) /
    ((2 : ℝ) ^ w) ^ t

/-- Encoding of an LWE instance `(A, b)`: `[n, m, q]`, `A` row-major, then `b`. -/
def lweEnc (n m q : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) (b : Fin m → ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  [n, m, q] ++
    List.ofFn (fun t : Fin (m * n) =>
      ((A (finProdFinEquiv.symm t).1 (finProdFinEquiv.symm t).2 : Fin q) : ℕ)) ++
    List.ofFn b

/-- `(A s + e) mod q`, with `e` given as natural numbers. -/
def lweRHS {n m q : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) (s : Fin n → Fin q) (e : Fin m → ℕ) :
    Fin m → ℕ :=
  fun i => ((∑ j : Fin n, ((A i j : Fin q) : ℕ) * ((s j : Fin q) : ℕ)) + e i) % q

/-- Admissible word sizes for all instances of shape `(n, m, q)`. -/
def AdmAll (wc n m q w : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) (b : Fin m → Fin q), WROK wc (lweEnc n m q A (fun (i : Fin _) => (b i : ℕ))) w

/-- Acceptance probability on uniform `(A, b)`. -/
def accUnif (prog : List WRInstr) (n m q w t : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((Fintype.card (Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((Fintype.card (Fin m → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    ∑ A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q, ∑ b : Fin m → Fin q,
      wrProb prog w t (lweEnc n m q A (fun (i : Fin _) => (b i : ℕ))) [1]

/-- Acceptance probability on binary-error LWE samples (`e` uniform in `{0,1}^m`). -/
def accBin (prog : List WRInstr) (n m q w t : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((Fintype.card (Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    ((2 : ℝ) ^ m)⁻¹ *
    ∑ A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q, ∑ s : Fin n → Fin q, ∑ e : Fin m → Bool,
      wrProb prog w t (lweEnc n m q A (lweRHS A s (fun (i : Fin _) => wrBit (e i)))) [1]

/-- Gaussian function `ρ_s(z) = exp(-π z² / s²)`. -/
def rho (s : ℝ) (z : ℤ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-Real.pi * (z : ℝ) ^ 2 / s ^ 2)

/-- Discrete Gaussian `D_{ℤ,s}` reduced mod `q`: probability of residue `e`. -/
def dgMod (s : ℝ) (q : ℕ) (e : Fin q) : ℝ :=
  (∑' z : ℤ, if z % (q : ℤ) = ((e : ℕ) : ℤ) then rho s z else 0) / (∑' z : ℤ, rho s z)

/-- Acceptance probability on standard LWE samples with discrete Gaussian error of width `s`. -/
def accGauss (prog : List WRInstr) (n m q w t : ℕ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Fintype.card (Fin m → Fin n → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin q) : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    ∑ A : Fin m → Fin n → Fin q, ∑ sec : Fin n → Fin q, ∑ e : Fin m → Fin q,
      (∏ i : Fin m, dgMod s q (e i)) *
        wrProb prog w t (lweEnc n m q A (lweRHS A sec (fun (i : Fin _) => ((e i : Fin q) : ℕ)))) [1]

/-- Non-negligible advantage: for some `d`, for infinitely many `n`, at every admissible word size the
advantage `adv n w` is at least `n^{-d}`. -/
def NonNegl (adm : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) (adv : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ ∀ w : ℕ, adm n w → 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ d ≤ adv n w

/-- `A` breaks binary-error LWE (`m = ⌈C n⌉`, modulus `q n`) with budget `O(T n)`. -/
def BinBreaks (C : ℝ) (q : ℕ → ℕ) (A : WRAlgo) (Cst : ℝ) (T : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  NonNegl (fun (n w : ℕ) => AdmAll A.wc n ⌈C * (n : ℝ)⌉₊ (q n) w)
    (fun (n w : ℕ) => |accBin A.prog n ⌈C * (n : ℝ)⌉₊ (q n) w (wrBudget Cst (T n)) -
                 accUnif A.prog n ⌈C * (n : ℝ)⌉₊ (q n) w (wrBudget Cst (T n))|)

/-- (a): a `2^{o(n)}`-time distinguisher for binary-error LWE. -/
def BinEasy (C : ℝ) (q : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f n / (n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ Cst : ℝ, BinBreaks C q A Cst (fun (n : ℕ) => (2 : ℝ) ^ (f n))

/-- Binary-error LWE is hard for polynomial time. -/
def BinHard (C : ℝ) (q : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : WRAlgo, ∀ Cst : ℝ, ∀ c : ℕ, ¬ BinBreaks C q A Cst (fun (n : ℕ) => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

/-- A family of standard LWE parameters indexed by the security parameter `n`. -/
structure LWEParams where
  dim : ℕ → ℕ
  modulus : ℕ → ℕ
  samples : ℕ → ℕ
  width : ℕ → ℝ

/-- Standard parameters: polynomially related dimension, polynomial modulus and sample count, Gaussian
width `s = αq' ≥ 2√n'`. -/
def StdParams (P : LWEParams) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
    2 ≤ P.modulus n ∧ P.modulus n ≤ n ^ c ∧ P.samples n ≤ n ^ c ∧
    1 ≤ P.dim n ∧ P.dim n ≤ n ^ c ∧ n ≤ P.dim n ^ c ∧
    2 * Real.sqrt (P.dim n : ℝ) ≤ P.width n

/-- Standard decision LWE with parameters `P` is hard for polynomial time. -/
def LWEHard (P : LWEParams) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : WRAlgo, ∀ Cst : ℝ, ∀ c : ℕ,
    ¬ NonNegl (fun (n w : ℕ) => AdmAll A.wc (P.dim n) (P.samples n) (P.modulus n) w)
      (fun (n w : ℕ) =>
        |accGauss A.prog (P.dim n) (P.samples n) (P.modulus n) w (wrBudget Cst ((n : ℝ) ^ c))
            (P.width n) -
          accUnif A.prog (P.dim n) (P.samples n) (P.modulus n) w (wrBudget Cst ((n : ℝ) ^ c))|)

/-- Dichotomy for binary-error LWE with `m = ⌈C n⌉` samples: for every `C > 1` and polynomially bounded
modulus, either a `2^{o(n)}` attack exists, or hardness follows from standard LWE. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ C : ℝ, 1 < C → ∀ q : ℕ → ℕ, (∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ q n ∧ q n ≤ n ^ c + c) →
    BinEasy C q ∨ ∃ P : LWEParams, StdParams P ∧ (LWEHard P → BinHard C q)

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM033

title: Densest k-Subgraph and k-Biclique FPT-inapproximability from plain ETH
credit: Chalermsook et al., From Gap-ETH to FPT-inapproximability, FOCS 2017 (arXiv:1708.04218); Feldmann, Karthik C.S., Lee, Manurangsi, survey on approximation in parameterized complexity 2020 (arXiv:2006.04411)
plain: Prove, assuming only ETH, that Densest k-Subgraph cannot be approximated within k^{o(1)} (or any omega(1) factor) in f(k) n^{o(k)} time, or that k-Biclique has no f(k)n^{o(sqrt k)}-type algorithm, matching known Gap-ETH-based results.

(Gap-ETH gives every g = k^{o(1)}; the k-Biclique disjunct is already known under ETH, Lin JACM 2018.)

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M034: Densest k-Subgraph and k-Biclique FPT-inapproximability from plain ETH
Prove, assuming only ETH (not Gap-ETH), that Densest k-Subgraph has no FPT approximation within some
factor g(k) = ω(1).
Informal statement: Assuming only (deterministic) ETH, prove that there is a function g(k) → ∞ such
that no algorithm running in time f(k)·n^{O(1)} (f computable) approximates (uncolored) Densest
k-Subgraph within factor g(k), i.e. outputs a value v with OPT/g(k) ≤ v ≤ OPT, where OPT is the maximum
number of edges induced by k vertices. (Gap-ETH gives this for every g(k) = k^{o(1)}: Chalermsook et al.,
FOCS 2017. The k-Biclique disjunct of the original W is already known under ETH: Lin, JACM 2018,
arXiv:1406.3700.)
Formalization notes:
* Reading of "any factor ω(1)": it must be "some ω(1) factor" (∃ g → ∞). The reading "for every g = ω(1)"
  is false, since a factor g(k) = k² (indeed k) is trivially achievable in polynomial time.
* Machine model: the board's canonical word-RAM block (pasted verbatim below); deterministic algorithms,
  time O(T) = ⌊C·T + C⌋ steps, for every admissible word size w ≥ (wc+1)·log(input length).
* 3-SAT / ETH: `CNF3` = n variables, clauses of ≤ 3 literals, encoded injectively as `[n, #clauses]` plus
  3 words per clause. `ETH` := ∃ δ > 0, ∀ c, no deterministic algorithm decides 3-SAT in time
  O(2^{δn}·L^c) (L = number of input words; the poly(L) factor is harmless since L ≤ poly(n) after removing
  duplicate clauses). This is the standard Impagliazzo–Paturi ETH.
* Densest k-Subgraph: an instance is (N, a Boolean N×N matrix, k); the graph has edge {i,j} (i ≠ j) iff
  `adjM i j || adjM j i` (so every matrix is a valid graph; loops ignored). Input encoding `[N, k]` plus the
  N² matrix bits (input size Θ(N²), polynomial in N). OPT = max over k-subsets S of the number of edges
  inside S (0 if k > N). A g-approximation outputs a single word v with OPT ≤ g(k)·v and v ≤ OPT. A value
  approximation is weaker than finding a dense set (from a set one counts its edges in poly time), so
  hardness for value approximation is the stronger (standard, gap-based) form.
* FPT time: f(k)·N^c with f : ℕ → ℕ computable (`Computable`, Mathlib) — the standard (strongly uniform)
  FPT notion used in the ETH/Gap-ETH literature.
* Claim := ETH → ∃ g : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 1 ≤ g k) ∧ g → ∞ ∧ ∀ f computable, ∀ c, no deterministic algorithm
  g-approximates DkS in time O(f(k)·N^c). ¬Claim would require proving ETH (¬(A→B) = A ∧ ¬B), so it is
  unreachable without resolving ETH, as usual for conditional hardness. Loophole audit: g ≥ 1 makes the
  output condition satisfiable (v = OPT), brute force solves DkS exactly in time N^{O(k)}, so the model
  is not empty; g is chosen before f, c and the algorithm.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM034
noncomputable section

/-! ### Canonical word-RAM model (QED board, shared block; paste verbatim inside the problem namespace)

* A machine has word size `w`; every register and memory cell holds a natural number `< 2^w`
  (invariant: every register write is reduced mod `2^w`; memory only receives register values
  and input words, which are required to be `< 2^w`).
* Registers `R : ℕ → ℕ` (a program mentions only finitely many) and memory `M : ℕ → ℕ`
  (addresses are register values, hence `< 2^w`: at most `2^w` cells, all initially 0 except input).
* Program: a finite list of the standard unit-cost instructions below; `pc` indexes the list.
  A `pc` outside the list (in particular after `halt`, or a jump past the end) means halted, and a
  halted configuration is a fixed point of `wrStep`.
* Input: a list of words `x₀ … x_{n-1}` placed in `M[0..n-1]`; initially `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`,
  all other registers 0. Output: on halting, `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`.
* Randomness: instruction `rand d` reads the next word of a random tape (word `k` is
  `tape k mod 2^w`). Deterministic runs use the all-zero tape.
* Cost: one step per instruction. `RunsWithin` asks the machine to be halted after `t` steps.
* Word size: an algorithm carries a constant `wc`, and must be correct for EVERY word size
  `w ≥ (wc+1)·(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` for which all input words fit (`< 2^w`). Requiring all such `w`
  (rather than letting the algorithm pick `w`) rules out the "huge word" loophole: the time bound
  must already hold at `w = Θ(log n)`, while larger `w` never hurts (the program can mask).
-/

/-- The instruction set (all unit cost). Indices `d a b` are register names, `t` a program address. -/
inductive WRInstr where
  /-- `R d := c mod 2^w` (a fixed program constant). -/
  | const (d c : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := M[R a]` (indirect load). -/
  | load (d a : ℕ)
  /-- `M[R a] := R s` (indirect store). -/
  | store (a s : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a + R b) mod 2^w`. -/
  | add (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := R a - R b`, truncated at 0. -/
  | sub (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a * R b) mod 2^w` (low word of the product). -/
  | mul (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := ⌊R a / R b⌋` (and `x / 0 = 0`). -/
  | div (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Bitwise and / or / xor. -/
  | band (d a b : ℕ)
  | bor (d a b : ℕ)
  | bxor (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a · 2^(R b)) mod 2^w` and `R d := ⌊R a / 2^(R b)⌋`. -/
  | shl (d a b : ℕ)
  | shr (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Unconditional jump; jump if `R a = 0`; jump if `R a < R b`. -/
  | jmp (t : ℕ)
  | jz (a t : ℕ)
  | jlt (a b t : ℕ)
  /-- `R d :=` next random word. -/
  | rand (d : ℕ)
  /-- Stop. -/
  | halt

/-- Machine configuration: program counter, registers, memory, number of random words used. -/
structure WRCfg where
  pc : ℕ
  reg : ℕ → ℕ
  mem : ℕ → ℕ
  rc : ℕ

/-- One step of program `prog` with word size `w` and random tape `tape`. -/
def wrStep (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (s : WRCfg) : WRCfg :=
  match prog[s.pc]? with
  | none => s
  | some ins =>
    let upd : ℕ → ℕ → WRCfg := fun d v =>
      { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (v % 2 ^ w) }
    let jump : Bool → ℕ → WRCfg := fun b t =>
      { s with pc := if b then t else s.pc + 1 }
    match ins with
    | .const d c => upd d c
    | .load d a => upd d (s.mem (s.reg a))
    | .store a r => { s with pc := s.pc + 1, mem := Function.update s.mem (s.reg a) (s.reg r) }
    | .add d a b => upd d (s.reg a + s.reg b)
    | .sub d a b => upd d (s.reg a - s.reg b)
    | .mul d a b => upd d (s.reg a * s.reg b)
    | .div d a b => upd d (s.reg a / s.reg b)
    | .band d a b => upd d (Nat.land (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bor d a b => upd d (Nat.lor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bxor d a b => upd d (Nat.xor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .shl d a b => upd d (s.reg a * 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .shr d a b => upd d (s.reg a / 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .jmp t => { s with pc := t }
    | .jz a t => jump (decide (s.reg a = 0)) t
    | .jlt a b t => jump (decide (s.reg a < s.reg b)) t
    | .rand d =>
        { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (tape s.rc % 2 ^ w), rc := s.rc + 1 }
    | .halt => { s with pc := prog.length }

/-- Initial configuration: input in `M[0..n-1]`, `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`. -/
def wrInit (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) : WRCfg where
  pc := 0
  reg := fun i => if i = 0 then input.length else if i = 1 then w else 0
  mem := fun a => input.getD a 0
  rc := 0

/-- Output of a configuration: `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`. -/
def wrOutput (s : WRCfg) : List ℕ := (List.range (s.reg 0)).map s.mem

/-- Halted: the program counter has left the program. -/
def WRHalted (prog : List WRInstr) (s : WRCfg) : Prop := prog.length ≤ s.pc

/-- With random tape `tape`, the run on `input` has halted after `t` steps (i.e. within `t` steps,
since halted configurations are fixed points) with output `out`. -/
def RunsWithinR (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ)
    (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) ∧
    wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) = out

/-- Deterministic run (all-zero random tape). -/
def RunsWithin (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  RunsWithinR prog w (fun _ => 0) input t out

/-- An algorithm: a program and a word-size constant `wc` (it may assume `w ≥ (wc+1)·log n`). -/
structure WRAlgo where
  prog : List WRInstr
  wc : ℕ

/-- Admissible word sizes for an input: `w ≥ (wc+1)(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` (so `n < 2^w`) and every
input word fits in `w` bits. -/
def WROK (wc : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (w : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (wc + 1) * (Nat.log 2 (input.length + 1) + 1) ≤ w ∧ ∀ x ∈ input, x < 2 ^ w

/-- The step budget `⌊C·T + C⌋₊` used for "time O(T)" (the additive `C` absorbs small inputs). -/
def wrBudget (C T : ℝ) : ℕ := ⌊C * T + C⌋₊

/-- A (batch) problem: instances, a word encoding of each instance, and the set of correct outputs. -/
structure WRProblem where
  Inst : Type
  enc : Inst → List ℕ
  Correct : Inst → List ℕ → Prop

/-- Deterministic: some algorithm solves every instance `x` within `O(T x)` steps, for every
admissible word size. (`T` may depend on any parameters of the instance.) -/
def WRSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithin A.prog w (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧ P.Correct x out

/-- The random tape determined by `L` random `w`-bit words (word `k ≥ L` reads as 0; a run of `L`
steps reads at most `L` words, so uniform `f` is exactly a uniformly random tape). -/
def wrTape {L w : ℕ} (f : Fin L → Fin (2 ^ w)) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  fun k => if h : k < L then (f ⟨k, h⟩ : ℕ) else 0

/-- Randomized (Monte Carlo, worst-case time): for every instance and admissible `w`, at least 2/3
of the random tapes make the algorithm halt within `O(T x)` steps with a correct output. -/
def WRRandSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (T x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (T x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithinR A.prog w (wrTape f) (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧
          P.Correct x out}

/-! #### Online (multi-phase) variant
Phase inputs `x₀, x₁, …` arrive one at a time. Before phase `j` the words of `x_j` overwrite
`M[0..|x_j|-1]`, `R 0 := |x_j|`, `pc := 0`; all other registers, memory and the random-tape position
persist. The phase's output is read when it halts. Phase `j` cannot see `x_{j+1}`, so answers are
online. Inputs are fixed in advance (oblivious adversary). -/

/-- Feed the next phase input into a (halted) configuration. -/
def wrFeed (s : WRCfg) (x : List ℕ) : WRCfg :=
  { s with pc := 0, reg := Function.update s.reg 0 x.length,
           mem := fun a => if a < x.length then x.getD a 0 else s.mem a }

/-- `wrPhases prog w tape s xs ts os`: starting from `s`, phase `j` gets input `xs[j]`, halts within
`ts[j]` steps and outputs `os[j]`. -/
def wrPhases (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) :
    WRCfg → List (List ℕ) → List ℕ → List (List ℕ) → Prop
  | _, [], [], [] => True
  | s, x :: xs, t :: ts, o :: os =>
      WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) ∧
      wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) = o ∧
      wrPhases prog w tape ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) xs ts os
  | _, _, _, _ => False

/-- An online problem: instances, the list of phase inputs, and correct lists of phase outputs. -/
structure WROnlineProblem where
  Inst : Type
  phases : Inst → List (List ℕ)
  Correct : Inst → List (List ℕ) → Prop

/-- All words of all phases. -/
def wrAllWords (xs : List (List ℕ)) : List ℕ := xs.foldr (· ++ ·) []

/-- Randomized online solution with first-phase (preprocessing) time `O(Tpre x)` and total time of
all later phases `O(Tq x)` (so amortized time per later phase is `Tq x / (#phases - 1)`). -/
def WROnlineRandSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
          wrPhases A.prog w (wrTape f) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
          (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
          P.Correct x outs}

/-- Deterministic online solution (all-zero tape). -/
def WROnlineSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
      wrPhases A.prog w (fun _ => 0) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
      (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
      P.Correct x outs

/-! #### Encoding helpers -/

/-- Boolean as a word. -/
def wrBit (b : Bool) : ℕ := cond b 1 0

/-- Integer as a word (zig-zag: `z ≥ 0 ↦ 2z`, `z < 0 ↦ 2|z| + 1`). -/
def wrInt (z : ℤ) : ℕ := 2 * z.natAbs + (if z < 0 then 1 else 0)

/-- A list of pairs as a flat list of words. -/
def wrPairs : List (ℕ × ℕ) → List ℕ
  | [] => []
  | p :: l => p.1 :: p.2 :: wrPairs l

/-- Output `out` is the yes/no answer to `b`: `[1]` if `b`, `[0]` otherwise. -/
def WRAnswer (b : Prop) (out : List ℕ) : Prop := (b ∧ out = [1]) ∨ (¬ b ∧ out = [0])

/-! ### 3-SAT and ETH -/

/-- A 3-CNF formula on `n` variables: each clause is a list of at most 3 literals (variable, sign). -/
structure CNF3 where
  n : ℕ
  clauses : List (List (Fin n × Bool))
  short : ∀ cl ∈ clauses, cl.length ≤ 3

/-- Satisfiability. -/
def CNF3.Sat (φ : CNF3) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : Fin φ.n → Bool, ∀ cl ∈ φ.clauses, ∃ l ∈ cl, σ l.1 = l.2

/-- Literal code `2(v+1) + sign` (never 0). -/
def litCode {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n × Bool) : ℕ := 2 * ((l.1 : ℕ) + 1) + wrBit l.2

/-- A clause as exactly 3 words (padded with 0). -/
def clauseCode {n : ℕ} (cl : List (Fin n × Bool)) : List ℕ :=
  (cl.map litCode ++ [0, 0, 0]).take 3

/-- Word encoding of a formula. -/
def CNF3.enc (φ : CNF3) : List ℕ :=
  [φ.n, φ.clauses.length] ++ wrAllWords (φ.clauses.map clauseCode)

/-- The decision problem 3-SAT. -/
def SAT3 : WRProblem where
  Inst := CNF3
  enc := CNF3.enc
  Correct := fun (φ : CNF3) (out : List ℕ) => WRAnswer φ.Sat out

/-- ETH: for some `δ > 0`, no deterministic algorithm decides 3-SAT in time `O(2^{δ n} · L^c)`. -/
def ETH : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ c : ℕ,
    ¬ WRSolvesIn SAT3 (fun φ : CNF3 => (2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (φ.n : ℝ)) * ((φ.enc.length : ℝ)) ^ c)

/-! ### Densest k-Subgraph -/

/-- An instance: a graph on `Fin N` given by a Boolean matrix (edge `{i,j}`, `i ≠ j`, iff
`adjM i j || adjM j i`), and the parameter `k`. -/
structure DkSInst where
  N : ℕ
  adjM : Fin N → Fin N → Bool
  k : ℕ

/-- Number of edges inside `S`. -/
def DkSInst.edgesIn (x : DkSInst) (S : Finset (Fin x.N)) : ℕ :=
  ((S ×ˢ S).filter (fun p : Fin x.N × Fin x.N =>
    p.1 < p.2 ∧ (x.adjM p.1 p.2 || x.adjM p.2 p.1) = true)).card

/-- `OPT`: the maximum number of edges induced by `k` vertices (0 if `k > N`). -/
def DkSInst.opt (x : DkSInst) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin x.N)).powersetCard x.k).sup x.edgesIn

/-- Encoding: `[N, k]` followed by the `N²` matrix bits, row-major. -/
def DkSInst.enc (x : DkSInst) : List ℕ :=
  [x.N, x.k] ++
    List.ofFn (fun t : Fin (x.N * x.N) =>
      wrBit (x.adjM (finProdFinEquiv.symm t).1 (finProdFinEquiv.symm t).2))

/-- `g`-approximate Densest k-Subgraph (value version): output one word `v`, `OPT ≤ g(k)·v ≤ g(k)·OPT`. -/
def DkSApprox (g : ℕ → ℝ) : WRProblem where
  Inst := DkSInst
  enc := DkSInst.enc
  Correct := fun (x : DkSInst) (out : List ℕ) =>
    ∃ v : ℕ, out = [v] ∧ (x.opt : ℝ) ≤ g x.k * (v : ℝ) ∧ v ≤ x.opt

/-- ETH implies: for some approximation factor `g(k) → ∞`, Densest k-Subgraph has no FPT
`g(k)`-approximation algorithm. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ETH → ∃ g : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ g k) ∧ Filter.Tendsto g Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
    ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Computable f → ∀ c : ℕ,
      ¬ WRSolvesIn (DkSApprox g) (fun x : DkSInst => (f x.k : ℝ) * (x.N : ℝ) ^ c)

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM034
prov_reason: ETH-based (rather than Gap-ETH) FPT-inapproximability of Densest k-Subgraph is a listed open question in the parameterized-approximation literature.

title: Does UGC imply SSEH?
credit: Raghavendra, Steurer, 'Graph expansion and the Unique Games Conjecture', STOC 2010; Raghavendra, Steurer, Tulsiani, 'Reductions between expansion problems', CCC 2012 (arXiv:1011.2586)
plain: Give a polynomial-time reduction from Small-Set Expansion to Unique Games' hardness direction, i.e. prove UGC => SSEH (Raghavendra-Steurer proved SSEH => UGC), or exhibit an oracle/algorithmic separation (e.g. an algorithm for SSE on a class of graphs where UG remains as hard as in general).
math: Prove that Small-Set Expansion is UG-hard: for every η > 0 there are δ ∈ (0,1) and ε > 0 such that for every alphabet size q there is a polynomial-time many-one reduction from Gap-UG_q(1−ε, ε) (YES: some labelling satisfies ≥ 1−ε of the constraints; NO: none satisfies more than ε) to Gap-SSE(η, δ) on regular graphs (YES: some vertex set of measure δ has expansion ≤ η; NO: every vertex set of measure δ has expansion ≥ 1−η). Such reductions give UGC ⇒ SSEH (Raghavendra–Steurer proved SSEH ⇒ UGC). Separations in restricted models (oracles, SoS) are not part of the statement.
refs: Raghavendra, Steurer, Graph expansion and the Unique Games Conjecture, STOC 2010
Raghavendra, Steurer, Tulsiani, Reductions between expansion problems, CCC 2012, arXiv:1011.2586
Bafna, Barak, Kothari, Schramm, Steurer, Playing Unique Games on certified small-set expanders, STOC 2021, arXiv:2006.09969
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M035: Does UGC imply SSEH?
Give a polynomial-time reduction from Unique Games to Small-Set Expansion, i.e. prove UGC ⇒ SSEH
(Raghavendra–Steurer proved SSEH ⇒ UGC), or exhibit a separation in an explicit model.
Informal statement: Prove that Small-Set Expansion is UG-hard: for every η > 0 there are
δ ∈ (0,1) and ε > 0 such that for every alphabet size q there is a polynomial-time many-one
reduction from Gap-UG_q(1−ε, ε) to Gap-SSE(η, δ). Here Gap-UG_q(1−ε, ε) means: YES if some
labelling satisfies ≥ 1−ε of the constraints, NO if none satisfies more than ε. Gap-SSE(η, δ)
means, for regular graphs: YES if some vertex set of measure δ has expansion ≤ η, NO if every
vertex set of measure δ has expansion ≥ 1−η. Such reductions give UGC ⇒ SSEH. A separation is
only meaningful in a restricted model and is not part of Claim.
Formalization notes:
* `UGInstance q` (as in QED-M028): n variables, m constraints, the e-th constraint is
  `perm e (f (src e)) = f (dst e)`. `value f` is the satisfied fraction (0 if m = 0, so empty
  instances are NO instances).
* `SGraph` is an undirected multigraph given as an edge list (self-loops allowed, counted twice in
  degrees). `IsRegular` means n ≥ 1 and all degrees are equal to some r ≥ 1. μ(S) = |S|/n and
  Φ(S) = |∂S| / vol(S), where vol(S) = ∑_{v∈S} deg v = r|S| and ∂S is the set of edges with exactly
  one endpoint in S. This is the Raghavendra–Steurer(–Tulsiani) formulation with exact measure δ.
  Both YES and NO instances must be regular, so the promise sets are disjoint for η < 1/2.
* Polynomial time: instances are encoded as bit strings (`encUG`, `encG`) using self-delimiting
  unary numerals (polynomially related to the natural instance size). A reduction is a map
  R : UGInstance q → SGraph together with a function F : List Bool → List Bool that is
  `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` (Mathlib's polynomial-time multi-stack Turing machines, with
  the identity encoding of `List Bool` over the alphabet `Bool`) and satisfies
  F (encUG I) = encG (R I).
* Quantifiers: δ and ε depend only on η, and the reduction may depend on q. UGC gives, for each
  ε, some q = q(ε) with Gap-UG_q(1−ε, ε) NP-hard, so Claim ⇒ (UGC ⇒ SSEH). Requiring the reduction
  for every q is necessary. Otherwise q = 1, where every instance with m > 0 has value 1, would
  give a trivial reduction (test m = 0).
* Claim also follows from unconditional NP-hardness of Gap-SSE(η, δ), since Gap-UG_q is a promise
  problem in NP. The bare implication "UGC ⇒ SSEH" is not used as Claim because it is vacuously
  true if UGC is false.
Proving `Claim` = such reductions (SSE is UG-hard). Proving `¬Claim` = for some η > 0 no
(δ, ε) has polynomial-time reductions for all q. That would in particular imply P ≠ NP (if
P = NP, every promise problem in NP reduces to any non-trivial one), so the negative direction is
out of reach unconditionally, as expected.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM035
noncomputable section

/-! ### Unique Games -/

/-- A Unique Games instance over alphabet `Fin q`. -/
structure UGInstance (q : ℕ) where
  n : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  src : Fin m → Fin n
  dst : Fin m → Fin n
  perm : Fin m → Equiv.Perm (Fin q)

/-- Fraction of constraints satisfied by the labelling `f`. -/
def UGInstance.value {q : ℕ} (I : UGInstance q) (f : Fin I.n → Fin q) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin I.m => I.perm e (f (I.src e)) = f (I.dst e))).card : ℝ) /
    (I.m : ℝ)

/-- YES instances of Gap-UG(1−ε, ε). -/
def UGYes {q : ℕ} (ε : ℝ) (I : UGInstance q) : Prop := ∃ f : Fin I.n → Fin q, 1 - ε ≤ I.value f

/-- NO instances of Gap-UG(1−ε, ε). -/
def UGNo {q : ℕ} (ε : ℝ) (I : UGInstance q) : Prop := ∀ f : Fin I.n → Fin q, I.value f ≤ ε

/-! ### Small-Set Expansion -/

/-- An undirected multigraph as an edge list. -/
structure SGraph where
  n : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  src : Fin m → Fin n
  dst : Fin m → Fin n

/-- Degree (a self-loop contributes 2). -/
def SGraph.deg (G : SGraph) (v : Fin G.n) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun e : Fin G.m => G.src e = v).card +
    (Finset.univ.filter fun e : Fin G.m => G.dst e = v).card

/-- Nonempty and `r`-regular for some `r ≥ 1`. -/
def SGraph.IsRegular (G : SGraph) : Prop :=
  0 < G.n ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ v : Fin G.n, G.deg v = r

/-- Number of edges leaving `S`. -/
def SGraph.boundary (G : SGraph) (S : Finset (Fin G.n)) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun e : Fin G.m =>
    (G.src e ∈ S ∧ G.dst e ∉ S) ∨ (G.src e ∉ S ∧ G.dst e ∈ S)).card

/-- Volume of `S`. -/
def SGraph.vol (G : SGraph) (S : Finset (Fin G.n)) : ℕ := ∑ v ∈ S, G.deg v

/-- Edge expansion `Φ(S) = |∂S| / vol(S)`. -/
def SGraph.expansion (G : SGraph) (S : Finset (Fin G.n)) : ℝ :=
  (G.boundary S : ℝ) / (G.vol S : ℝ)

/-- Uniform measure `|S| / n`. -/
def SGraph.measure (G : SGraph) (S : Finset (Fin G.n)) : ℝ := (S.card : ℝ) / (G.n : ℝ)

/-- YES instances of Gap-SSE(η, δ). -/
def SSEYes (η δ : ℝ) (G : SGraph) : Prop :=
  G.IsRegular ∧ ∃ S : Finset (Fin G.n), G.measure S = δ ∧ G.expansion S ≤ η

/-- NO instances of Gap-SSE(η, δ). -/
def SSENo (η δ : ℝ) (G : SGraph) : Prop :=
  G.IsRegular ∧ ∀ S : Finset (Fin G.n), G.measure S = δ → 1 - η ≤ G.expansion S

/-! ### Encodings and polynomial time -/

/-- Self-delimiting unary numeral. -/
def unary (k : ℕ) : List Bool := List.replicate k true ++ [false]

/-- Concatenation of a list of bit strings. -/
def concatL : List (List Bool) → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | l :: t => l ++ concatL t

/-- Encoding of a Unique Games instance. -/
def encUG {q : ℕ} (I : UGInstance q) : List Bool :=
  unary I.n ++ unary I.m ++
    concatL (List.ofFn fun e : Fin I.m =>
      unary (I.src e).val ++ unary (I.dst e).val ++
        concatL (List.ofFn fun i : Fin q => unary (I.perm e i).val))

/-- Encoding of a graph. -/
def encG (G : SGraph) : List Bool :=
  unary G.n ++ unary G.m ++
    concatL (List.ofFn fun e : Fin G.m => unary (G.src e).val ++ unary (G.dst e).val)

/-- Bit strings encoded as themselves over the alphabet `Bool`. -/
def listBoolEnc : Computability.FinEncoding (List Bool) where
  Γ := Bool
  encode := id
  decode := Option.some
  decode_encode := fun _ => rfl
  ΓFin := (inferInstance : Fintype Bool)

/-- `F` is computable in polynomial time by a Mathlib multi-stack Turing machine. -/
def PolyTimeFn (F : List Bool → List Bool) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime listBoolEnc listBoolEnc F)

/-- Small-Set Expansion is UG-hard. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ < 1 ∧ ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ q : ℕ,
    ∃ (R : UGInstance q → SGraph) (F : List Bool → List Bool),
      PolyTimeFn F ∧ (∀ I : UGInstance q, F (encUG I) = encG (R I)) ∧
      (∀ I : UGInstance q, UGYes ε I → SSEYes η δ (R I)) ∧
      (∀ I : UGInstance q, UGNo ε I → SSENo η δ (R I))

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM035
M_fix_reason: M is not a statement: it lists two outcomes ('Equivalence ... Separation ...') and their consequences. Also, an unconditional 'separation' cannot be proved without proving UGC, so the precise question is the existence of a UG-to-SSE reduction, with separations only in restricted models.
prov_reason: Whether Unique Games is hard for Small-Set Expansion (the converse of SSEH ⇒ UGC) is the standing question raised by Raghavendra-Steurer and Raghavendra-Steurer-Tulsiani.

title: Finding Huang's vertex
results: The PPP-hardness reduction is correct. Take n=m+2. Pad 2^m real pigeons with 2^m+1 dummies, mapped injectively to the 2^m+1 dummy holes. Send the pigeon with C(x)=0 to dummy hole #1, so a collision with dummy #1 decodes to a zero-solution. Embed holes as h -> (h, parity h), which gives even weight. No two even-weight strings are adjacent, so every solution is a collision that decodes to a PIGEON solution.
plain: Huang's theorem says that any set of more than half the corners of the n-cube contains a corner with at least √n neighbours in the set. When the set is listed by a small circuit, how hard is it to find such a corner, or a flaw in the listing? The problem is easily shown to be at least as hard as the pigeonhole class PPP. Is it in PPP, so that it is PPP-complete, or does Huang's linear-algebra proof make it harder?
math: HUANG (black-box form): the input is the table of f : [2^{n-1}+1] → {0,1}^n, read bit by bit. Output either i ≠ j in [2^{n-1}+1] with f(i) = f(j), or i, j_1, …, j_m in [2^{n-1}+1] with m = ⌈√n⌉ such that f(j_1),…,f(j_m) are distinct and each is at Hamming distance 1 from f(i). Claim: HUANG ∈ PPP^dt, i.e. there is a constant c such that for every n, HUANG_n reduces to PIGEON_m with m ≤ (n+2)^c by a decision-tree reduction of depth ≤ (n+2)^c. Every PIGEON input bit is a depth-bounded decision tree on the HUANG input, and every PIGEON solution maps back to a HUANG solution by such a tree. (The white-box circuit version follows from a uniform such reduction. The white-box negative answer would imply FP ≠ PPP. Which class contains HUANG if Claim fails is a follow-up and not part of Claim.)
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M036: Finding Huang's vertex
Huang's theorem says that any set of more than half the corners of the n-cube contains a corner
with at least √n neighbours in the set. When the set is listed by a small circuit, how hard is it
to find such a corner, or a flaw in the listing? The problem is easily shown to be at least as hard
as the pigeonhole class PPP. Is it in PPP, so that it is PPP-complete, or does Huang's
linear-algebra proof make it harder?
Informal statement: HUANG: given a Boolean circuit f : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^n with inputs read as
elements of [2^{n-1}+1] (others ignored), output either i ≠ j in [2^{n-1}+1] with f(i) = f(j), or
i, j_1, …, j_m in [2^{n-1}+1] with m = ⌈√n⌉ such that f(j_1),…,f(j_m) are distinct and each is at
Hamming distance 1 from f(i). Is HUANG ∈ PPP (under polynomial-time reductions; or, in the
black-box model, is it reducible to PIGEON)? If not, which standard TFNP class contains it, and is
it complete for it?
Formalization notes: Claim is the black-box (query / decision-tree) form of "HUANG ∈ PPP", i.e.
HUANG ∈ PPP^dt in the sense of Göös–Kamath–Robere–Sokolov and later TFNP^dt papers.
* Black-box HUANG_n: the input is the table of f : [2^{n-1}+1] → {0,1}^n, accessed bit by bit;
  input bits are indexed by `Dom n × Fin n` (`Dom n = Fin (2^(n-1)+1)`), so the input length is
  N = (2^{n-1}+1)·n and polylog(N) = poly(n). Solutions (`HSol`, `IsHSol`) are exactly the two kinds
  in the informal statement; ⌈√n⌉ is `ceilSqrt n` (integer ceiling of the square root). The witnesses
  must lie in the domain. HUANG_n is total: if f is injective its image has 2^{n-1}+1 > 2^n/2
  vertices, and by Huang some image vertex has ≥ √n, hence ≥ ⌈√n⌉, neighbours in the image.
* Black-box PIGEON_m: input table of g : {0,1}^m → {0,1}^m; solutions are z with g(z) = 0^m or
  z ≠ z' with g(z) = g(z').
* `DTree`: ordinary Boolean decision trees; depth = number of queries on the longest path.
* A depth-d reduction from HUANG_n to PIGEON_m (`DTReduction`): every bit of the PIGEON_m instance
  is computed by a depth-≤d decision tree on the HUANG_n input, and every candidate PIGEON solution
  s is mapped by a depth-≤d decision tree to a HUANG_n solution; `Correct` requires that for every
  input x, whenever s is a valid solution of the derived instance, the tree's output is a valid
  solution for x. This is the standard many-one decision-tree reduction.
* PPP^dt membership: reductions with m ≤ polylog(N) PIGEON bits (i.e. 2^{polylog N} pigeons) and
  depth polylog(N). Since log N = Θ(n), Claim asks for m ≤ (n+2)^c and depth ≤ (n+2)^c for one c
  and every n.
Proving `Claim` = a black-box reduction of HUANG to PIGEON (a uniform such reduction also gives
white-box HUANG ∈ PPP). Proving `¬Claim` = a query-complexity separation: for every c there is n
with no such reduction, i.e. HUANG ∉ PPP^dt (the white-box negative form would imply FP ≠ PPP and
is out of reach unconditionally). PPP-hardness (the converse reduction) is known and recorded in
the problem's results; the follow-up "which class contains it" is not part of Claim.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM036
noncomputable section

/-- Boolean decision trees querying bits indexed by `α`, with leaves labelled in `γ`.
`node a t₀ t₁` queries bit `a` and continues in `t₀` if it is `false`, in `t₁` if `true`. -/
inductive DTree (α : Type) (γ : Type) : Type where
  | leaf : γ → DTree α γ
  | node : α → DTree α γ → DTree α γ → DTree α γ

/-- Evaluation of a decision tree on the input `x`. -/
def DTree.eval {α γ : Type} (x : α → Bool) : DTree α γ → γ
  | DTree.leaf c => c
  | DTree.node a t₀ t₁ => if x a = true then DTree.eval x t₁ else DTree.eval x t₀

/-- Depth (number of queries on the longest root-leaf path). -/
def DTree.depth {α γ : Type} : DTree α γ → ℕ
  | DTree.leaf _ => 0
  | DTree.node _ t₀ t₁ => max (DTree.depth t₀) (DTree.depth t₁) + 1

/-- `⌈√n⌉` as a natural number. -/
def ceilSqrt (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt n + if Nat.sqrt n * Nat.sqrt n = n then 0 else 1

/-- Vertices of the n-cube. -/
abbrev Cube (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin n → Bool

/-- Hamming distance. -/
def hamming {n : ℕ} (u v : Cube n) : ℕ := (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin n => u k ≠ v k).card

/-- The domain `[2^{n-1}+1]` of the listing. -/
abbrev Dom (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin (2 ^ (n - 1) + 1)

/-- Bit positions of a black-box HUANG_n input: bit `k` of `f(i)`. -/
abbrev HIn (n : ℕ) : Type := Dom n × Fin n

/-- The listing `f` encoded by the input bits `x`. -/
def hf {n : ℕ} (x : HIn n → Bool) (i : Dom n) : Cube n := fun k => x (i, k)

/-- Candidate HUANG_n solutions: a collision `(i, j)`, or a vertex index `i` with `⌈√n⌉` indices. -/
abbrev HSol (n : ℕ) : Type := (Dom n × Dom n) ⊕ (Dom n × (Fin (ceilSqrt n) → Dom n))

/-- Validity of a HUANG_n solution. -/
def IsHSol {n : ℕ} (x : HIn n → Bool) : HSol n → Prop
  | Sum.inl (i, j) => i ≠ j ∧ hf x i = hf x j
  | Sum.inr (i, J) =>
      Function.Injective (fun k : Fin (ceilSqrt n) => hf x (J k)) ∧
        ∀ k : Fin (ceilSqrt n), hamming (hf x i) (hf x (J k)) = 1

/-- Bit positions of a black-box PIGEON_m input: bit `k` of `g(z)`. -/
abbrev PIn (m : ℕ) : Type := Cube m × Fin m

/-- The map `g` encoded by the input bits `y`. -/
def pg {m : ℕ} (y : PIn m → Bool) (z : Cube m) : Cube m := fun k => y (z, k)

/-- Candidate PIGEON_m solutions: a preimage of `0^m`, or a collision. -/
abbrev PSol (m : ℕ) : Type := Cube m ⊕ (Cube m × Cube m)

/-- Validity of a PIGEON_m solution. -/
def IsPSol {m : ℕ} (y : PIn m → Bool) : PSol m → Prop
  | Sum.inl z => pg y z = fun _ => false
  | Sum.inr (z, z') => z ≠ z' ∧ pg y z = pg y z'

/-- A decision-tree reduction from HUANG_n to PIGEON_m. -/
structure DTReduction (n m : ℕ) where
  /-- each PIGEON input bit as a decision tree over the HUANG input -/
  bit : PIn m → DTree (HIn n) Bool
  /-- each PIGEON solution mapped back by a decision tree -/
  sol : PSol m → DTree (HIn n) (HSol n)

/-- All trees of the reduction have depth at most `d`. -/
def DTReduction.DepthLE {n m : ℕ} (R : DTReduction n m) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ p : PIn m, (R.bit p).depth ≤ d) ∧ ∀ s : PSol m, (R.sol s).depth ≤ d

/-- Correctness: valid PIGEON solutions of the derived instance map to valid HUANG solutions. -/
def DTReduction.Correct {n m : ℕ} (R : DTReduction n m) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : HIn n → Bool) (s : PSol m),
    IsPSol (fun p : PIn m => DTree.eval x (R.bit p)) s → IsHSol x (DTree.eval x (R.sol s))

/-- HUANG ∈ PPP^dt: polylog(N) = poly(n) size and depth decision-tree reductions to PIGEON. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, m ≤ (n + 2) ^ c ∧
    ∃ R : DTReduction n m, R.DepthLE ((n + 2) ^ c) ∧ R.Correct

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM036

credit: Korten (FOCS 2021); Chen, Hirahara, Ren (STOC 2024), arXiv:2309.12912; Li (STOC 2024), arXiv:2310.17762.
premise_risks: ECCC TR26-118 (Ren–Williams, Jul 2026, unrefereed): status claim that E^{prMA}/1 requires 2^n/n circuits; only affects the 'state of the art' summary, not the statement.
arXiv:2605.03306 (Hitchcock, May 2026 preprint): comeagerness result in S₂E; context only.

math: Prove that for some ε > 0 there is L ∈ E^NP such that for infinitely many n, L ∩ {0,1}^n has no circuit of size 2^{εn} (stronger: for all large n). Related target (not claimed equivalent at this size): AVOID ∈ FP^NP, which by Korten (2021) implies E^NP ⊄ SIZE[2^n/n].
refs: Chen, Hirahara, Ren, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size, STOC 2024, arXiv:2309.12912
Li, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size: simplified, truly uniform, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.17762

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M037: From S_2E to E^NP: near-maximum circuit lower bounds
Chen–Hirahara–Ren and Li showed that symmetric exponential time S₂E requires near-maximum
circuit size. The next target is E^NP: show that some language in E^NP needs circuits of
exponential size.
Informal statement: Prove that for some ε > 0 there is L ∈ E^NP such that for infinitely many n,
L ∩ {0,1}^n has no Boolean circuit of size 2^{εn} (stronger: for all large n). Related target (not
claimed equivalent at this size): AVOID ∈ FP^NP, which by Korten (2021) implies
E^NP ⊄ SIZE[2^n/n].
Formalization notes:
* Circuits: straight-line programs over the basis {AND, OR, NOT} (fan-in 2, NOT ignores its
  second argument). Wires 0..n−1 are the inputs, and gate i is wire n+i. `WellFormed` forces every
  gate to read only earlier wires. The output is the last wire. Size = number of gates. Exponential
  lower bounds are insensitive to the choice of finite complete basis.
* Machines: Mathlib's `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` on `List Bool` (identity encoding over
  the alphabet `Bool`).
* NP (`InNP`): O(x) ↔ ∃ y, |y| ≤ |x|^k + k, V(⟨x, y⟩) = [true] with V polynomial-time. ⟨·,·⟩ is
  the injective pairing `pairEnc` (bit-doubling of x, then a separator).
* E^NP (`InENP`) in transcript form. Fix O ∈ NP, a constant c and a polynomial-time M. On input x
  (n = |x|) the oracle computation proceeds in rounds. With the answer string a (initially empty),
  M is run on ⟨x, ⟨a, 1^{2^{cn}}⟩⟩. Output `false :: z` means "query z": the bit O(z) is appended
  to a. Output `true :: b :: _` means "halt with answer b" (absorbing). L ∈ E^NP iff for every x
  the computation halts within 2^{cn} rounds with answer [x ∈ L]. This is equivalent to the
  standard definition E^NP = ⋃_c DTIME^{SAT}(2^{cn}):
  (⊆) a 2^{cn}-time SAT-oracle machine makes ≤ 2^{cn} queries. M replays it for 2^{cn} steps using
  the recorded answers and outputs its next query or its result, in time poly(2^{cn}) =
  poly(input length), thanks to the padding 1^{2^{cn}}. Take O = SAT ∈ NP.
  (⊇) an oracle machine for SAT runs the rounds, at 2^{O(n)} rounds × 2^{O(n)} time each. Queries
  to O ∈ NP of length 2^{O(n)} reduce to SAT queries of length 2^{O(n)}.
  The padding is essential. Without it M would be polynomial in n, not exponential.
* Lower bound: `Claim` = ∃ ε > 0, ∃ L ∈ E^NP, for infinitely many n no well-formed circuit with
  ≤ 2^{εn} gates computes L on all strings of length n (input bit j = j-th list entry).
Proving `Claim` = the exponential circuit lower bound for E^NP (the i.o. version). Proving
`¬Claim` = for every ε > 0 every E^NP language has circuits of size ≤ 2^{εn} for all large n
(not expected, and itself a major result). The a.e. version and Korten's AVOID formulation are
not part of Claim.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM037
noncomputable section

/-! ### Boolean circuits -/

/-- Gate types. -/
inductive GateOp : Type where
  | andG : GateOp
  | orG : GateOp
  | notG : GateOp

/-- A gate reading wires `a` and `b` (`notG` ignores `b`). -/
structure Gate where
  op : GateOp
  a : ℕ
  b : ℕ

/-- The function computed by a gate. -/
def Gate.apply (g : Gate) (u v : Bool) : Bool :=
  match g.op with
  | GateOp.andG => u && v
  | GateOp.orG => u || v
  | GateOp.notG => !u

/-- All wire values: the inputs followed by the gate values in order. -/
def evalWires (x : List Bool) (C : List Gate) : List Bool :=
  C.foldl (fun vals g => vals ++ [g.apply (vals.getD g.a false) (vals.getD g.b false)]) x

/-- Gate `i` reads only inputs and earlier gates. -/
def WellFormed (n : ℕ) (C : List Gate) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin C.length, (C.get i).a < n + i.val ∧ (C.get i).b < n + i.val

/-- Output of the circuit: the last wire. -/
def circOut (x : List Bool) (C : List Gate) : Bool :=
  (evalWires x C).getD ((evalWires x C).length - 1) false

/-- `L` restricted to length `n` has a circuit with at most `s` gates. -/
def HasCircuit (L : List Bool → Prop) (n : ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : List Gate, WellFormed n C ∧ (C.length : ℝ) ≤ s ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool, x.length = n → (circOut x C = true ↔ L x)

/-! ### Polynomial time, NP and E^NP -/

/-- Bit strings encoded as themselves over the alphabet `Bool`. -/
def listBoolEnc : Computability.FinEncoding (List Bool) where
  Γ := Bool
  encode := id
  decode := Option.some
  decode_encode := fun _ => rfl
  ΓFin := (inferInstance : Fintype Bool)

/-- `F` is computable in polynomial time by a Mathlib multi-stack Turing machine. -/
def PolyTimeFn (F : List Bool → List Bool) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime listBoolEnc listBoolEnc F)

/-- Bit doubling `b ↦ true b`. -/
def dbl : List Bool → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | b :: t => true :: b :: dbl t

/-- Injective pairing of bit strings. -/
def pairEnc (x y : List Bool) : List Bool := dbl x ++ [false] ++ y

/-- `O` is in NP. -/
def InNP (O : List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (V : List Bool → List Bool) (k : ℕ), PolyTimeFn V ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool, O x ↔ ∃ y : List Bool, y.length ≤ x.length ^ k + k ∧ V (pairEnc x y) = [true]

/-- The input of the round machine: `x`, the answers so far, and padding `1^{2^{c|x|}}`. -/
def roundInput (c : ℕ) (x ans : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEnc x (pairEnc ans (List.replicate (2 ^ (c * x.length)) true))

open Classical in
/-- The oracle answers collected after `t` rounds. -/
def answers (M : List Bool → List Bool) (O : List Bool → Prop) (c : ℕ) (x : List Bool) :
    ℕ → List Bool
  | 0 => []
  | t + 1 =>
      match M (roundInput c x (answers M O c x t)) with
      | false :: z => answers M O c x t ++ [decide (O z)]
      | _ => answers M O c x t

/-- `some b` if the machine has halted with answer `b` at round `t`. -/
def haltBit (M : List Bool → List Bool) (O : List Bool → Prop) (c : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    Option Bool :=
  match M (roundInput c x (answers M O c x t)) with
  | true :: b :: _ => some b
  | _ => none

/-- `L ∈ E^NP` (transcript form, see the notes). -/
def InENP (L : List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ O : List Bool → Prop, InNP O ∧ ∃ c : ℕ, ∃ M : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeFn M ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t : ℕ, t ≤ 2 ^ (c * x.length) ∧
      ∃ b : Bool, haltBit M O c x t = some b ∧ (L x ↔ b = true)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∃ L : List Bool → Prop, InENP L ∧
    ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ ¬ HasCircuit L n ((2 : ℝ) ^ (ε * (n : ℝ)))

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM037

title: How fast does eps_k vanish for k-OV in low dimension?
credit: Dürr, Kipouridis, Lampis, Węgrzycki, 'Faster algorithms for k-Orthogonal Vectors in low dimension', ICALP 2026, arXiv:2507.11098; Björklund–Kaski, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.11926.
plain: Dürr-Kipouridis-Lampis-Węgrzycki show k-OV is solvable in O(2^{(1-eps_k)d} n) for every fixed k, and that eps_k -> 0 is forced by the Set Cover Conjecture. Determine the decay rate: prove eps_k >= c/log k (or c/k), or show that eps_k >= omega(1/k) would refute the Set Cover Conjecture.
math: Prove or disprove: there are absolute constants c > 0 and p ∈ ℕ such that for every k ≥ 2, k-OV on k sets of n vectors in {0,1}^d is solvable by a deterministic word-RAM algorithm in time O_k(2^{(1 - c/ln k) d} · n^p). (The exponent p must not depend on k: otherwise brute force n^k·d makes the statement trivial. Companion SCC direction is separate.)
refs: Dürr, Kipouridis, Lampis, Węgrzycki, Faster algorithms for k-Orthogonal Vectors in low dimension, ICALP 2026, arXiv:2507.11098
Björklund, Kaski, The Asymptotic Rank Conjecture and the Set Cover Conjecture are not both true, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.11926

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M038: How fast does eps_k vanish for k-OV in low dimension?
Dürr–Kipouridis–Lampis–Węgrzycki (ICALP 2026) solve k-Orthogonal Vectors in O(2^{(1−ε_k)d}·n)
time for every fixed k, and show that under the Set Cover Conjecture (SCC) the savings ε_k must
tend to 0. Determine how fast: is ε_k ≥ c/log k (or ≥ c/k) achievable, or does SCC force
ε_k = O(1/k)?
Informal statement (sharpened): Prove or disprove: there are an absolute constant c > 0 and an
absolute exponent p ∈ ℕ such that for every k ≥ 2, k-OV (given k sets of n vectors each in
{0,1}^d, decide whether one can pick one vector from each set so that every coordinate is 0 in at
least one picked vector) is solvable by a deterministic word-RAM algorithm in time
O_k(2^{(1 − c/ln k)·d} · n^p). (Companion direction, not part of Claim: SCC implies no
O(2^{(1−ε)d}·n^{O(1)}) algorithm for k-OV when ε ≥ C/k.)
Formalization notes: Uses the shared QED word-RAM block (WordRAM, pasted below): unit-cost
standard instructions on w-bit words, algorithm correct for every w ≥ (wc+1)·log₂(input length),
time O(T) = ⌊C·T + C⌋ steps; here the algorithm and C may depend on k (O_k), but c and p may not.
Sharpening: the original "n^{O(1)}" must have its exponent independent of k, otherwise the
statement is trivial (brute force n^k·d is n^{O(1)} for each fixed k); DKLW have p = 1. The base of
the logarithm only rescales c. Input (`OVInst.enc`): `[n, d]` then the k·n·d bits, set-major,
then vector, then coordinate. Output `[1]` iff an orthogonal k-tuple exists, else `[0]`.
Proving `Claim` = the algorithm with savings c/log k; `¬Claim` = for every c, p some k has no such
algorithm (an unconditional lower bound; in practice only SCC-conditional evidence is expected).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM038

noncomputable section

/-! ### Canonical word-RAM model (QED board, shared block; paste verbatim inside the problem namespace)

* A machine has word size `w`; every register and memory cell holds a natural number `< 2^w`
  (invariant: every register write is reduced mod `2^w`; memory only receives register values
  and input words, which are required to be `< 2^w`).
* Registers `R : ℕ → ℕ` (a program mentions only finitely many) and memory `M : ℕ → ℕ`
  (addresses are register values, hence `< 2^w`: at most `2^w` cells, all initially 0 except input).
* Program: a finite list of the standard unit-cost instructions below; `pc` indexes the list.
  A `pc` outside the list (in particular after `halt`, or a jump past the end) means halted, and a
  halted configuration is a fixed point of `wrStep`.
* Input: a list of words `x₀ … x_{n-1}` placed in `M[0..n-1]`; initially `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`,
  all other registers 0. Output: on halting, `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`.
* Randomness: instruction `rand d` reads the next word of a random tape (word `k` is
  `tape k mod 2^w`). Deterministic runs use the all-zero tape.
* Cost: one step per instruction. `RunsWithin` asks the machine to be halted after `t` steps.
* Word size: an algorithm carries a constant `wc`, and must be correct for EVERY word size
  `w ≥ (wc+1)·(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` for which all input words fit (`< 2^w`). Requiring all such `w`
  (rather than letting the algorithm pick `w`) rules out the "huge word" loophole: the time bound
  must already hold at `w = Θ(log n)`, while larger `w` never hurts (the program can mask).
-/

/-- The instruction set (all unit cost). Indices `d a b` are register names, `t` a program address. -/
inductive WRInstr where
  /-- `R d := c mod 2^w` (a fixed program constant). -/
  | const (d c : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := M[R a]` (indirect load). -/
  | load (d a : ℕ)
  /-- `M[R a] := R s` (indirect store). -/
  | store (a s : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a + R b) mod 2^w`. -/
  | add (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := R a - R b`, truncated at 0. -/
  | sub (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a * R b) mod 2^w` (low word of the product). -/
  | mul (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := ⌊R a / R b⌋` (and `x / 0 = 0`). -/
  | div (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Bitwise and / or / xor. -/
  | band (d a b : ℕ)
  | bor (d a b : ℕ)
  | bxor (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- `R d := (R a · 2^(R b)) mod 2^w` and `R d := ⌊R a / 2^(R b)⌋`. -/
  | shl (d a b : ℕ)
  | shr (d a b : ℕ)
  /-- Unconditional jump; jump if `R a = 0`; jump if `R a < R b`. -/
  | jmp (t : ℕ)
  | jz (a t : ℕ)
  | jlt (a b t : ℕ)
  /-- `R d :=` next random word. -/
  | rand (d : ℕ)
  /-- Stop. -/
  | halt

/-- Machine configuration: program counter, registers, memory, number of random words used. -/
structure WRCfg where
  pc : ℕ
  reg : ℕ → ℕ
  mem : ℕ → ℕ
  rc : ℕ

/-- One step of program `prog` with word size `w` and random tape `tape`. -/
def wrStep (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (s : WRCfg) : WRCfg :=
  match prog[s.pc]? with
  | none => s
  | some ins =>
    let upd : ℕ → ℕ → WRCfg := fun d v =>
      { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (v % 2 ^ w) }
    let jump : Bool → ℕ → WRCfg := fun b t =>
      { s with pc := if b then t else s.pc + 1 }
    match ins with
    | .const d c => upd d c
    | .load d a => upd d (s.mem (s.reg a))
    | .store a r => { s with pc := s.pc + 1, mem := Function.update s.mem (s.reg a) (s.reg r) }
    | .add d a b => upd d (s.reg a + s.reg b)
    | .sub d a b => upd d (s.reg a - s.reg b)
    | .mul d a b => upd d (s.reg a * s.reg b)
    | .div d a b => upd d (s.reg a / s.reg b)
    | .band d a b => upd d (Nat.land (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bor d a b => upd d (Nat.lor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .bxor d a b => upd d (Nat.xor (s.reg a) (s.reg b))
    | .shl d a b => upd d (s.reg a * 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .shr d a b => upd d (s.reg a / 2 ^ (s.reg b))
    | .jmp t => { s with pc := t }
    | .jz a t => jump (decide (s.reg a = 0)) t
    | .jlt a b t => jump (decide (s.reg a < s.reg b)) t
    | .rand d =>
        { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d (tape s.rc % 2 ^ w), rc := s.rc + 1 }
    | .halt => { s with pc := prog.length }

/-- Initial configuration: input in `M[0..n-1]`, `R 0 = n`, `R 1 = w`. -/
def wrInit (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) : WRCfg where
  pc := 0
  reg := fun i => if i = 0 then input.length else if i = 1 then w else 0
  mem := fun a => input.getD a 0
  rc := 0

/-- Output of a configuration: `M[0 .. R 0 - 1]`. -/
def wrOutput (s : WRCfg) : List ℕ := (List.range (s.reg 0)).map s.mem

/-- Halted: the program counter has left the program. -/
def WRHalted (prog : List WRInstr) (s : WRCfg) : Prop := prog.length ≤ s.pc

/-- With random tape `tape`, the run on `input` has halted after `t` steps (i.e. within `t` steps,
since halted configurations are fixed points) with output `out`. -/
def RunsWithinR (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ)
    (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) ∧
    wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrInit w input)) = out

/-- Deterministic run (all-zero random tape). -/
def RunsWithin (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (t : ℕ) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  RunsWithinR prog w (fun _ => 0) input t out

/-- An algorithm: a program and a word-size constant `wc` (it may assume `w ≥ (wc+1)·log n`). -/
structure WRAlgo where
  prog : List WRInstr
  wc : ℕ

/-- Admissible word sizes for an input: `w ≥ (wc+1)(⌊log₂(n+1)⌋+1)` (so `n < 2^w`) and every
input word fits in `w` bits. -/
def WROK (wc : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) (w : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (wc + 1) * (Nat.log 2 (input.length + 1) + 1) ≤ w ∧ ∀ x ∈ input, x < 2 ^ w

/-- The step budget `⌊C·T + C⌋₊` used for "time O(T)" (the additive `C` absorbs small inputs). -/
def wrBudget (C T : ℝ) : ℕ := ⌊C * T + C⌋₊

/-- A (batch) problem: instances, a word encoding of each instance, and the set of correct outputs. -/
structure WRProblem where
  Inst : Type
  enc : Inst → List ℕ
  Correct : Inst → List ℕ → Prop

/-- Deterministic: some algorithm solves every instance `x` within `O(T x)` steps, for every
admissible word size. (`T` may depend on any parameters of the instance.) -/
def WRSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithin A.prog w (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧ P.Correct x out

/-- The random tape determined by `L` random `w`-bit words (word `k ≥ L` reads as 0; a run of `L`
steps reads at most `L` words, so uniform `f` is exactly a uniformly random tape). -/
def wrTape {L w : ℕ} (f : Fin L → Fin (2 ^ w)) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  fun k => if h : k < L then (f ⟨k, h⟩ : ℕ) else 0

/-- Randomized (Monte Carlo, worst-case time): for every instance and admissible `w`, at least 2/3
of the random tapes make the algorithm halt within `O(T x)` steps with a correct output. -/
def WRRandSolvesIn (P : WRProblem) (T : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (P.enc x) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (T x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (T x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ out : List ℕ, RunsWithinR A.prog w (wrTape f) (P.enc x) (wrBudget C (T x)) out ∧
          P.Correct x out}

/-! #### Online (multi-phase) variant
Phase inputs `x₀, x₁, …` arrive one at a time. Before phase `j` the words of `x_j` overwrite
`M[0..|x_j|-1]`, `R 0 := |x_j|`, `pc := 0`; all other registers, memory and the random-tape position
persist. The phase's output is read when it halts. Phase `j` cannot see `x_{j+1}`, so answers are
online. Inputs are fixed in advance (oblivious adversary). -/

/-- Feed the next phase input into a (halted) configuration. -/
def wrFeed (s : WRCfg) (x : List ℕ) : WRCfg :=
  { s with pc := 0, reg := Function.update s.reg 0 x.length,
           mem := fun a => if a < x.length then x.getD a 0 else s.mem a }

/-- `wrPhases prog w tape s xs ts os`: starting from `s`, phase `j` gets input `xs[j]`, halts within
`ts[j]` steps and outputs `os[j]`. -/
def wrPhases (prog : List WRInstr) (w : ℕ) (tape : ℕ → ℕ) :
    WRCfg → List (List ℕ) → List ℕ → List (List ℕ) → Prop
  | _, [], [], [] => True
  | s, x :: xs, t :: ts, o :: os =>
      WRHalted prog ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) ∧
      wrOutput ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) = o ∧
      wrPhases prog w tape ((wrStep prog w tape)^[t] (wrFeed s x)) xs ts os
  | _, _, _, _ => False

/-- An online problem: instances, the list of phase inputs, and correct lists of phase outputs. -/
structure WROnlineProblem where
  Inst : Type
  phases : Inst → List (List ℕ)
  Correct : Inst → List (List ℕ) → Prop

/-- All words of all phases. -/
def wrAllWords (xs : List (List ℕ)) : List ℕ := xs.foldr (· ++ ·) []

/-- Randomized online solution with first-phase (preprocessing) time `O(Tpre x)` and total time of
all later phases `O(Tq x)` (so amortized time per later phase is `Tq x / (#phases - 1)`). -/
def WROnlineRandSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    2 * (2 ^ w) ^ (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) ≤
      3 * Nat.card {f : Fin (wrBudget C (Tpre x) + wrBudget C (Tq x)) → Fin (2 ^ w) //
        ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
          wrPhases A.prog w (wrTape f) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
          (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
          P.Correct x outs}

/-- Deterministic online solution (all-zero tape). -/
def WROnlineSolvesIn (P : WROnlineProblem) (Tpre Tq : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : WRAlgo, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : P.Inst, ∀ w : ℕ, WROK A.wc (wrAllWords (P.phases x)) w →
    ∃ ts : List ℕ, ∃ outs : List (List ℕ),
      wrPhases A.prog w (fun _ => 0) (wrInit w []) (P.phases x) ts outs ∧
      (ts.take 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tpre x) ∧ (ts.drop 1).sum ≤ wrBudget C (Tq x) ∧
      P.Correct x outs

/-! #### Encoding helpers -/

/-- Boolean as a word. -/
def wrBit (b : Bool) : ℕ := cond b 1 0

/-- Integer as a word (zig-zag: `z ≥ 0 ↦ 2z`, `z < 0 ↦ 2|z| + 1`). -/
def wrInt (z : ℤ) : ℕ := 2 * z.natAbs + (if z < 0 then 1 else 0)

/-- A list of pairs as a flat list of words. -/
def wrPairs : List (ℕ × ℕ) → List ℕ
  | [] => []
  | p :: l => p.1 :: p.2 :: wrPairs l

/-- Output `out` is the yes/no answer to `b`: `[1]` if `b`, `[0]` otherwise. -/
def WRAnswer (b : Prop) (out : List ℕ) : Prop := (b ∧ out = [1]) ∨ (¬ b ∧ out = [0])

/-! ### Problem-specific definitions -/

/-- A k-OV instance: `vec i a j` is coordinate `j < d` of vector `a < n` of set `i < k`. -/
structure OVInst (k : ℕ) where
  n : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  vec : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Bool

/-- Encoding: `[n, d]` then all bits, set-major, then vector, then coordinate. -/
def OVInst.enc {k : ℕ} (x : OVInst k) : List ℕ :=
  [x.n, x.d] ++
    (List.range (k * x.n * x.d)).map
      (fun t => wrBit (x.vec (t / (x.n * x.d)) ((t / x.d) % x.n) (t % x.d)))

/-- There is a choice of one vector per set whose coordinatewise product is the zero vector. -/
def OVInst.Yes {k : ℕ} (x : OVInst k) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ i : ℕ, i < k → f i < x.n) ∧
    ∀ j : ℕ, j < x.d → ∃ i : ℕ, i < k ∧ x.vec i (f i) j = false

/-- The k-OV decision problem. -/
def KOV (k : ℕ) : WRProblem where
  Inst := OVInst k
  enc := fun (x : OVInst k) => x.enc
  Correct := fun (x : OVInst k) (out : List ℕ) => WRAnswer x.Yes out

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k →
    WRSolvesIn (KOV k)
      (fun (x : OVInst k) => (2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 - c / Real.log k) * (x.d : ℝ)) * (x.n : ℝ) ^ p)

end

end OpenProblems.QEDM038

title: Matching lower bound for OMv on low-VC-dimension matrices
credit: Anand, van den Brand, McCarty, 'The Structural Complexity of Matrix-Vector Multiplication', NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.21240; OMv conjecture: Henzinger, Krinninger, Nanongkai, Saranurak (STOC 2015).
plain: Anand-van den Brand-McCarty give O~(n^2) preprocessing and O~(n^{2-1/d}) query time for Boolean Mv when M has VC-dimension d. Show, assuming OMv (or unconditionally in the cell-probe model), that n^{2-c/d} query time is necessary for some constant c, for d up to some omega(1) function; or improve the upper bound to n^{2-f(d)} with f(d) >> 1/d.
math: Assume the OMv conjecture (no randomized word-RAM algorithm solves OMv in total time O(n^{3-ε}) for any ε > 0). Prove there are c > 0 and D(n) → ∞ such that for every d(n) with 1 ≤ d(n) ≤ D(n), every ε > 0 and every p, no randomized algorithm with O(n^p) preprocessing answers the n online Boolean matrix-vector queries for n×n matrices of VC-dimension ≤ d(n) in total query time O(n^{3-c/d(n)-ε}) (amortized n^{2-c/d(n)-ε} per query). (Positive alternative is a separate question.)
refs: Anand, van den Brand, McCarty, The Structural Complexity of Matrix-Vector Multiplication, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.21240
Henzinger, Krinninger, Nanongkai, Saranurak, Unifying and strengthening hardness for dynamic problems via the OMv conjecture, STOC 2015
