import Mathlib
/-! QED-M087: Blow-up under a steady force
Can a smooth, compactly supported, time-independent force drive the incompressible Navier–Stokes
fluid on ℝ³, starting at rest, to a finite-time singularity?
Informal statement: Decide whether there is f ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ³;ℝ³), independent of t, such that the solution
of ∂_t u + (u·∇)u + ∇p = Δu + f, ∇·u = 0, u(·,0) = 0 on ℝ³ loses smoothness in finite time.
(Claim: such an f exists.)
Formalization notes: Following the Clay formulation, "loses smoothness in finite time" means there is
no global smooth solution: no pair (u, P) smooth on ℝ³ × [0,∞) (`ContDiffOn ℝ n` on {t ≥ 0} for every
n) with u(x,0) = 0, satisfying the equations pointwise for t > 0, with locally-in-time bounded energy
∫|u(x,t)|² dx (a steady force can make energy grow, so a uniform-in-time bound as in Clay's (A)/(B)
would be wrong here; the lintegral avoids Bochner-integral junk values). Smooth finite-energy
solutions are unique, so this matches blow-up of the unique local smooth solution. Gradient forces
are trivially excluded (u = 0, P = potential).
Proving `Claim` = exhibiting a steady C_c^∞ force with finite-time blow-up. Proving `¬Claim` = global
regularity from rest for every steady C_c^∞ force.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM087

/-- ℝ³. -/
abbrev R3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- Space-time ℝ³ × ℝ. -/
abbrev ST : Type := R3 × ℝ

/-- Spatial partial derivative ∂_j of a scalar field. -/
noncomputable def dx (j : Fin 3) (g : ST → ℝ) (z : ST) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ g z ((Pi.single j (1 : ℝ) : R3), (0 : ℝ))

/-- Time derivative of a scalar field. -/
noncomputable def dtt (g : ST → ℝ) (z : ST) : ℝ := fderiv ℝ g z ((0 : R3), (1 : ℝ))

/-- `(u, P)` is a global smooth locally-finite-energy solution from rest with steady force `f`. -/
def IsGlobalSmoothSolution (f : R3 → R3) (u : ST → R3) (P : ST → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ n u {z : ST | 0 ≤ z.2}) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ n P {z : ST | 0 ≤ z.2}) ∧
  (∀ x : R3, u (x, 0) = 0) ∧
  (∀ z : ST, 0 < z.2 → ∀ i : Fin 3,
    dtt (fun w => u w i) z + ∑ j : Fin 3, u z j * dx j (fun w => u w i) z + dx i P z =
      ∑ j : Fin 3, dx j (fun w => dx j (fun w' => u w' i) w) z + f z.1 i) ∧
  (∀ z : ST, 0 < z.2 → ∑ j : Fin 3, dx j (fun w => u w j) z = 0) ∧
  (∀ T : ℝ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ T →
    ∫⁻ x : R3, ENNReal.ofReal (∑ i : Fin 3, (u (x, t) i) ^ 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ f : R3 → R3, (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n f) ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
    ¬ ∃ (u : ST → R3) (P : ST → ℝ), IsGlobalSmoothSolution f u P

end OpenProblems.QEDM087
prov_reason: This is a time-independent-force strengthening of the forced (Clay-type, OpenAI-claimed) Navier-Stokes blow-up.

title: Critical NLS blow-up threshold on the cube surface
credit: Extension of Weinstein (Comm. Math. Phys. 1983) mass-critical threshold; related Strichartz work on flat cones by Ford and by Blair-Ford-Marzuola.
plain: In the plane, the focusing cubic Schrödinger equation needs at least the ground-state mass to blow up. On the surface of a cube, each corner is a cone with total angle 3π/2, which can hold a 'three-quarter' ground state. So the blow-up threshold should drop to three quarters of the planar one, and the claim is that it does exactly that.
math: Let $S$ be the surface of the unit cube with its flat metric, and let $\Delta$ be the Friedrichs extension of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $C_c^\infty(S\setminus\{\text{vertices}\})$. Let $Q$ be the ground state of $\Delta Q-Q+Q^3=0$ on $\mathbb R^2$, and put $m_*=\tfrac34\|Q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2$. For $iu_t+\Delta u+|u|^2u=0$ on $S$, prove: (i) every $u_0\in H^1(S)$ with $\|u_0\|_2^2<m_*$ gives a global (forward-in-time) $H^1$ solution; (ii) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $u_0\in H^1(S)$ with $m_*<\|u_0\|_2^2<m_*+\varepsilon$ whose solution blows up in finite time (its $H^1$ norm is unbounded on its maximal interval $[0,T)$, $T<\infty$). (Stronger, optional: blow-up data exist for every mass $m>m_*$; also decide whether there is blow-up at mass exactly $m_*$.)
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M088: Critical NLS blow-up threshold on the cube surface
For the focusing cubic NLS on the flat surface of the unit cube, each vertex is a cone of angle 3π/2, which should lower the mass threshold for blow-up from ‖Q‖² to (3/4)‖Q‖². Prove global existence below m_* = (3/4)‖Q‖²_{L²(R²)} and blow-up for masses arbitrarily close above.
Informal statement: Let $S$ be the surface of the unit cube with its flat metric, and let $\Delta$ be the Friedrichs extension of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $C_c^\infty(S\setminus\{\text{vertices}\})$. Let $Q$ be the ground state of $\Delta Q-Q+Q^3=0$ on $\mathbb R^2$, and put $m_*=\tfrac34\|Q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2$. For $iu_t+\Delta u+|u|^2u=0$ on $S$, prove: (i) every $u_0\in H^1(S)$ with $\|u_0\|_2^2<m_*$ gives a global (forward-in-time) $H^1$ solution; (ii) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $u_0\in H^1(S)$ with $m_*<\|u_0\|_2^2<m_*+\varepsilon$ whose solution blows up in finite time (its $H^1$ norm is unbounded on its maximal interval $[0,T)$, $T<\infty$). (Stronger, optional: blow-up data exist for every mass $m>m_*$; also decide whether there is blow-up at mass exactly $m_*$.)
Formalization notes: The cube-surface model (shared verbatim with QED-M012 and QED-M089): S = ∂[0,1]³ ⊂ ℝ³ as
six closed faces, each the image of the closed unit square under an affine isometric chart; functions
are u : ℝ³ → ℂ restricted to S (so edge traces match automatically); area measure = Σ_faces Lebesgue
on the open square. Core `IsTest` (continuous on S, smooth up to the edges on each closed face) is a
form core of the Friedrichs extension; `IsEigenpair`/`IsEigenbasis` describe an orthonormal eigenbasis
(e_n, lam_n) of A = −Δ_Friedrichs ≥ 0 via the weak form against the core (see M012 notes).
H¹(S) = form domain = D(A^{1/2}), with ‖v‖²_{H¹} = Σ (1 + lam_n)|⟨e_n, v⟩|² (`H1sq`); `InH1` requires
v ∈ L² and summability. NLS solution on a time interval J ∋ 0 (`SolOn`), Duhamel form in eigen-
coefficients a_n(t) = ⟨e_n, u(t)⟩: from u_t = iΔu + i|u|²u,
a_n(t) = e^{−i lam_n t} a_n(0) + i ∫_0^t e^{−i lam_n (t−τ)} ⟨e_n, |u(τ)|²u(τ)⟩ dτ,
with u ∈ C(J; H¹) (H¹-continuity of t ↦ u(t)), |u(τ)|²u(τ) ∈ L² (true for H¹ by Sobolev H¹ ⊂ L⁶ on S;
demanded so that the pairings are genuine integrals), and τ ↦ ⟨e_n, |u|²u⟩ continuous (true for
C(J;H¹) solutions; demanded so the interval integral is not a junk value). At t = 0 the coefficients
of u(0) and u₀ agree, so u(0) = u₀ in L². This is the standard notion of H¹ (energy) solution; such
solutions are unique (2D cubic NLS, Yudovich/Ogawa–Ozawa type argument on compact surfaces), so
"global solution exists" and "the maximal solution blows up" (`BlowsUp`: a solution on [0,T), T < ∞,
with unbounded H¹ norm) are the usual dichotomy. Time is forward (t ≥ 0). Ground state: Q : ℝ² → ℝ
smooth, positive, tending to 0 at infinity, solving ΔQ − Q + Q³ = 0 classically (Laplacian by iterated
partial derivatives), with Q² integrable; by Gidas–Ni–Nirenberg and Kwong it is unique up to
translation, so m_* = (3/4)∫Q² is well defined; `Claim` quantifies over all such Q and also asserts one
exists. ‖u₀‖²₂ is `normSq` (area normalization 1 per face, matching Lebesgue normalization on ℝ²).
`Claim` = (eigenbasis exists) ∧ (ground state exists) ∧ ∀ Q, ∀ eigenbasis, (i) ∧ (ii); the existence
conjuncts prevent vacuous truth. ¬Claim means a sub-threshold H¹ datum without a global solution, or
some ε with no blow-up datum of mass in (m_*, m_*+ε). The optional strengthenings are not encoded.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM088
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-! ### Shared model of the flat surface of the unit cube

`S = ∂[0,1]³ ⊂ ℝ³`. Each face is the image of the closed unit square under an affine isometric chart;
since all faces sit inside the same `ℝ³`, the edge identifications are those of the cube and
continuity on `S` is exactly "matching edge traces". -/

/-- Points of `ℝ³`. -/
abbrev P3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- The six faces: `(i, b)` is the face `{x ∈ [0,1]³ | x i = b}` (`false ↦ 0`, `true ↦ 1`). -/
abbrev Face : Type := Fin 3 × Bool

/-- The fixed coordinate value of a face. -/
def bval (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else 0

/-- Isometric affine chart of face `(i, b)`: `(s, t) ↦ x` with `x i = b`, `x (i+1) = s`, `x (i+2) = t`
(indices mod 3). -/
def chart (f : Face) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : P3 := fun m : Fin 3 =>
  if m = f.1 then bval f.2 else if m = f.1 + 1 then p.1 else p.2

/-- The closed unit square. -/
def cSq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The open unit square (faces are integrated over it; the boundary is Lebesgue-null). -/
def Sq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The cube surface `S = ∂[0,1]³`. -/
def S : Set P3 := ⋃ f : Face, chart f '' cSq

/-- Pull-back of a function on `ℝ³` to face `f`'s square. -/
def pull (u : P3 → ℂ) (f : Face) : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ := fun p => u (chart f p)

/-- Partial derivative in the first square coordinate. -/
def d1 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun s : ℝ => v (s, p.2)) p.1

/-- Partial derivative in the second square coordinate. -/
def d2 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun t : ℝ => v (p.1, t)) p.2

/-- Core of the Dirichlet form: functions continuous on `S` whose restriction to every closed face
is the restriction of a `C^∞` function on `ℝ²` (smooth up to the edges). -/
def IsTest (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u S ∧
    ∀ f : Face, ∃ g : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ, (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k g) ∧ Set.EqOn (pull u f) g cSq

/-- `u` is (a representative of) an element of `L²(S)` for the surface (area) measure. -/
def IsL2 (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Face, AEStronglyMeasurable (pull u f) (volume.restrict Sq) ∧
    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2) (volume.restrict Sq)

/-- `L²(S)` inner product, conjugate-linear in the first slot. -/
def ip (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (starRingEnd ℂ) (pull u f p) * pull v f p

/-- `‖u‖²_{L²(S)}` (the mass). -/
def normSq (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ := ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2

/-- Sesquilinear Dirichlet form `E(u,v) = ∫_S ⟨∇u, ∇v⟩`, computed face by face. -/
def dform (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq,
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d1 (pull u f) p) * d1 (pull v f) p +
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (d2 (pull u f) p) * d2 (pull v f) p)

/-- Energy `E(u) = ∫_S |∇u|²`. -/
def energy (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (‖d1 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2 + ‖d2 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2)

/-- `w` is a sequence in the core that converges to `e` in `L²` and is Cauchy for the energy, i.e.
it witnesses that `e` lies in the form domain `H¹(S)` (closure of the core in the form norm). -/
def Approximates (e : P3 → ℂ) (w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : ℕ, IsTest (w m)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => normSq (w m - e)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m l : ℕ, N ≤ m → N ≤ l → energy (w m - w l) < ε

/-- `e` is an eigenfunction of the Friedrichs Laplacian `A = -Δ ≥ 0` with eigenvalue `lam`:
`e ∈ H¹(S)` and `E(e, φ) = lam ⟨e, φ⟩` for every `φ` in the core. -/
def IsEigenpair (lam : ℝ) (e : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  IsL2 e ∧ ∃ w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ, Approximates e w ∧
    ∀ φ : P3 → ℂ, IsTest φ →
      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => dform (w m) φ) atTop (𝓝 ((lam : ℂ) * ip e φ))

/-- An orthonormal eigenbasis of `L²(S)` for the Friedrichs Laplacian (eigenvalues of `-Δ`,
listed with multiplicity in any order). Completeness is Parseval's identity on the dense core. -/
def IsEigenbasis (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, IsEigenpair (lam n) (e n)) ∧
    (∀ n m : ℕ, ip (e n) (e m) = if n = m then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ u : P3 → ℂ, IsTest u → HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ‖ip (e n) u‖ ^ 2) (normSq u)

/-- `‖v‖²_{H¹(S)} = Σ (1 + lam_n) |⟨e_n, v⟩|²`. -/
def H1sq (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) (v : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n : ℕ, (1 + lam n) * ‖ip (e n) v‖ ^ 2

/-- `v ∈ H¹(S)` (the form domain of the Friedrichs Laplacian). -/
def InH1 (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) (v : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  IsL2 v ∧ Summable (fun n : ℕ => (1 + lam n) * ‖ip (e n) v‖ ^ 2)

/-- The cubic nonlinearity `|v|² v`. -/
def cubic (v : P3 → ℂ) : P3 → ℂ := fun x => ((‖v x‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * v x

/-- `u` is an `H¹` solution of `i u_t + Δu + |u|²u = 0`, `u(0) = u₀`, on the time interval `J ∋ 0`,
in Duhamel form on the eigen-coefficients. -/
def SolOn (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) (J : Set ℝ) (u0 : P3 → ℂ) (u : ℝ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (0 : ℝ) ∈ J ∧
  (∀ t ∈ J, InH1 lam e (u t) ∧ IsL2 (cubic (u t))) ∧
  (∀ t₀ ∈ J, Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => H1sq lam e (u t - u t₀)) (𝓝[J] t₀) (𝓝 0)) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, ContinuousOn (fun τ : ℝ => ip (e n) (cubic (u τ))) J) ∧
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ t ∈ J,
    ip (e n) (u t) =
      Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (lam n : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) * ip (e n) u0 +
        Complex.I * ∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..t,
          Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (lam n : ℂ) * ((t - τ : ℝ) : ℂ))) * ip (e n) (cubic (u τ))

/-- Finite-time blow-up: an `H¹` solution on `[0,T)`, `T < ∞`, whose `H¹` norm is unbounded. -/
def BlowsUp (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) (u0 : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : ℝ, 0 < T ∧ ∃ u : ℝ → P3 → ℂ, SolOn lam e (Set.Ico 0 T) u0 u ∧
    ¬ BddAbove ((fun t : ℝ => H1sq lam e (u t)) '' Set.Ico 0 T)

/-- Laplacian on `ℝ²` by iterated classical partial derivatives. -/
def lap2 (Q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=
  deriv (fun a : ℝ => deriv (fun a' : ℝ => Q (a', x.2)) a) x.1 +
    deriv (fun b : ℝ => deriv (fun b' : ℝ => Q (x.1, b')) b) x.2

/-- `Q` is a ground state of `ΔQ − Q + Q³ = 0` on `ℝ²` (positive, decaying, smooth). -/
def IsGroundState (Q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k Q) ∧ (∀ x : ℝ × ℝ, 0 < Q x) ∧
    Tendsto Q (cocompact (ℝ × ℝ)) (𝓝 0) ∧
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ × ℝ => Q x ^ 2) ∧
    ∀ x : ℝ × ℝ, lap2 Q x - Q x + Q x ^ 3 = 0

/-- Sharp threshold `m_* = (3/4) ‖Q‖²` for the focusing cubic NLS on the cube surface. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  (∃ (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ), IsEigenbasis lam e) ∧
  (∃ Q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, IsGroundState Q) ∧
  ∀ Q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, IsGroundState Q →
    ∀ (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ), IsEigenbasis lam e →
      let mstar : ℝ := 3 / 4 * ∫ x : ℝ × ℝ, Q x ^ 2
      (∀ u0 : P3 → ℂ, InH1 lam e u0 → normSq u0 < mstar →
          ∃ u : ℝ → P3 → ℂ, SolOn lam e (Set.Ici 0) u0 u) ∧
      (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ u0 : P3 → ℂ, InH1 lam e u0 ∧
          mstar < normSq u0 ∧ normSq u0 < mstar + ε ∧ BlowsUp lam e u0)

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM088
prov_reason: Transfers Weinstein's sharp mass threshold for planar mass-critical NLS to a cone-singular surface with a new explicit constant; no source poses the cube-surface version.

title: Derivative loss in L4 Strichartz on the cube surface
credit: Blair, Ford, Marzuola, Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on flat cones / Euclidean surfaces with conical singularities, arXiv:1003.0666.
results: s* >= 0 (trivial). No positive lower bound known. s* <= 1/4: Blair-Ford-Marzuola, Thm 1.5 (arXiv 1003.0666), loss 1/p for compact Euclidean surfaces with conical singularities, p=q=4; authors call the loss an artifact of the method.
plain: On the flat torus, the L4 space-time estimate for Schrodinger waves loses only epsilon derivatives (Bourgain). On the surface of a cube, which has eight cone points that diffract waves, only a loss of 1/4 derivative is known. Find the true loss: prove any loss below 1/4, or show some loss is necessary.
math: Let $S$ be the unit cube surface, $\Delta$ the Friedrichs extension from $C_c^\infty(S\setminus\text{vertices})$, and $s^*=\inf\{s\ge0:\|e^{it\Delta}f\|_{L^4([0,1]\times S)}\le C_s\|f\|_{H^s(S)}\}$. Known: $0\le s^*\le\tfrac14$ (Blair–Ford–Marzuola). Prove $s^*<\tfrac14$, or $s^*>0$; ideally determine $s^*$ (conjecturally $0$). The board's target (Claim) is $s^*<\tfrac14$.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M089: Derivative loss in L4 Strichartz on the cube surface
On the flat torus the L⁴ space-time Schrödinger estimate loses only ε derivatives (Bourgain). On the surface of a cube, which has eight cone points that diffract waves, only a loss of 1/4 derivative is known. Prove any loss below 1/4, or show some loss is necessary.
Informal statement: Let S be the unit cube surface, Δ the Friedrichs extension from C_c^∞(S \ vertices), and s* = inf{s ≥ 0 : ‖e^{itΔ}f‖_{L⁴([0,1]×S)} ≤ C_s‖f‖_{H^s(S)}}. Known: 0 ≤ s* ≤ 1/4 (Blair–Ford–Marzuola). Prove s* < 1/4, or s* > 0; ideally determine s* (conjecturally 0). The board's target (Claim) is s* < 1/4.
Formalization notes: The cube-surface model (shared verbatim with QED-M012 and QED-M088): S = ∂[0,1]³ ⊂ ℝ³ as
six closed faces, each the image of the closed unit square under an affine isometric chart; functions
are u : ℝ³ → ℂ restricted to S, so face functions automatically have matching edge traces; area
measure = Σ_faces Lebesgue on the open square. Core `IsTest` = continuous on S and smooth up to the
boundary on each closed face; it is a form core for the Friedrichs extension (it contains
C_c^∞(S \ vertices) and lies in H¹(S); points have zero capacity in 2D). H¹(S) membership is
witnessed by core sequences converging in L² and Cauchy in energy; `IsEigenpair lam e` is
e ∈ D(A), A e = lam e for A = −Δ_Friedrichs ≥ 0 (weak form against the core). `IsEigenbasis lam e` is
an orthonormal basis of L²(S) of such eigenfunctions (Parseval on the dense core gives completeness);
the spectrum is discrete, so this is the full spectral resolution. Schrödinger group:
e^{itΔ}(Σ c_n e_n) = Σ c_n e^{−it lam_n} e_n, and ‖f‖²_{H^s} = Σ (1 + lam_n)^s |c_n|² (H^s = D(A^{s/2})).
`StrichartzL4 lam e s C`: for every finitely supported coefficient vector c,
∫_0^1 ∫_S |e^{itΔ}f|⁴ ≤ C ‖f‖⁴_{H^s} (C is the 4th power of the constant C_s). Finite combinations of
eigenfunctions are dense in H^s and the L⁴ norm is lower semicontinuous under L² convergence (Fatou on a
subsequence), so the estimate on finite combinations is equivalent to the estimate on all of H^s; it
is also independent of which eigenbasis is used (both sides are basis-free on H^s). The space-time
integral is an `lintegral` of `ENNReal.ofReal (|·|⁴)`, so a non-integrable left side cannot make the
estimate hold by the Bochner junk value 0. `Claim` = existence of an eigenbasis (true; included so the
∀-basis clause is not vacuous) ∧ ∃ s ∈ [0, 1/4) such that for every eigenbasis the estimate holds with
some constant, i.e. s* < 1/4. Proving `¬Claim` means the BFM loss 1/4 is sharp: for every s < 1/4 the
estimate fails (it would show s* = 1/4). A positive lower bound s* > 0 is a different (also open)
statement and is not encoded.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM089
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-! ### Shared model of the flat surface of the unit cube

`S = ∂[0,1]³ ⊂ ℝ³`. Each face is the image of the closed unit square under an affine isometric chart;
since all faces sit inside the same `ℝ³`, the edge identifications are those of the cube and
continuity on `S` is exactly "matching edge traces". -/

/-- Points of `ℝ³`. -/
abbrev P3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- The six faces: `(i, b)` is the face `{x ∈ [0,1]³ | x i = b}` (`false ↦ 0`, `true ↦ 1`). -/
abbrev Face : Type := Fin 3 × Bool

/-- The fixed coordinate value of a face. -/
def bval (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else 0

/-- Isometric affine chart of face `(i, b)`: `(s, t) ↦ x` with `x i = b`, `x (i+1) = s`, `x (i+2) = t`
(indices mod 3). -/
def chart (f : Face) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : P3 := fun m : Fin 3 =>
  if m = f.1 then bval f.2 else if m = f.1 + 1 then p.1 else p.2

/-- The closed unit square. -/
def cSq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The open unit square (faces are integrated over it; the boundary is Lebesgue-null). -/
def Sq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The cube surface `S = ∂[0,1]³`. -/
def S : Set P3 := ⋃ f : Face, chart f '' cSq

/-- Pull-back of a function on `ℝ³` to face `f`'s square. -/
def pull (u : P3 → ℂ) (f : Face) : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ := fun p => u (chart f p)

/-- Partial derivative in the first square coordinate. -/
def d1 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun s : ℝ => v (s, p.2)) p.1

/-- Partial derivative in the second square coordinate. -/
def d2 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun t : ℝ => v (p.1, t)) p.2

/-- Core of the Dirichlet form: functions continuous on `S` whose restriction to every closed face
is the restriction of a `C^∞` function on `ℝ²` (smooth up to the edges). -/
def IsTest (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u S ∧
    ∀ f : Face, ∃ g : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ, (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k g) ∧ Set.EqOn (pull u f) g cSq

/-- `u` is (a representative of) an element of `L²(S)` for the surface (area) measure. -/
def IsL2 (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Face, AEStronglyMeasurable (pull u f) (volume.restrict Sq) ∧
    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2) (volume.restrict Sq)

/-- `L²(S)` inner product, conjugate-linear in the first slot. -/
def ip (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (starRingEnd ℂ) (pull u f p) * pull v f p

/-- `‖u‖²_{L²(S)}` (the mass). -/
def normSq (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ := ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2

/-- Sesquilinear Dirichlet form `E(u,v) = ∫_S ⟨∇u, ∇v⟩`, computed face by face. -/
def dform (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq,
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d1 (pull u f) p) * d1 (pull v f) p +
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (d2 (pull u f) p) * d2 (pull v f) p)

/-- Energy `E(u) = ∫_S |∇u|²`. -/
def energy (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (‖d1 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2 + ‖d2 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2)

/-- `w` is a sequence in the core that converges to `e` in `L²` and is Cauchy for the energy, i.e.
it witnesses that `e` lies in the form domain `H¹(S)` (closure of the core in the form norm). -/
def Approximates (e : P3 → ℂ) (w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : ℕ, IsTest (w m)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => normSq (w m - e)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m l : ℕ, N ≤ m → N ≤ l → energy (w m - w l) < ε

/-- `e` is an eigenfunction of the Friedrichs Laplacian `A = -Δ ≥ 0` with eigenvalue `lam`:
`e ∈ H¹(S)` and `E(e, φ) = lam ⟨e, φ⟩` for every `φ` in the core. -/
def IsEigenpair (lam : ℝ) (e : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  IsL2 e ∧ ∃ w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ, Approximates e w ∧
    ∀ φ : P3 → ℂ, IsTest φ →
      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => dform (w m) φ) atTop (𝓝 ((lam : ℂ) * ip e φ))

/-- An orthonormal eigenbasis of `L²(S)` for the Friedrichs Laplacian (eigenvalues of `-Δ`,
listed with multiplicity in any order). Completeness is Parseval's identity on the dense core. -/
def IsEigenbasis (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, IsEigenpair (lam n) (e n)) ∧
    (∀ n m : ℕ, ip (e n) (e m) = if n = m then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ u : P3 → ℂ, IsTest u → HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ‖ip (e n) u‖ ^ 2) (normSq u)

/-- The `L⁴([0,1] × S)` Strichartz estimate with `s` derivatives, for the eigenbasis `(lam, e)`:
`∫₀¹∫_S |e^{itΔ} f|⁴ ≤ C ‖f‖_{H^s}⁴` for all finite eigenfunction expansions `f = Σ_{n ∈ F} c n • e n`. -/
def StrichartzL4 (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) (s C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (F : Finset ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℂ),
    (∫⁻ t in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∑ f : Face, ∫⁻ p in Sq,
        ENNReal.ofReal (‖∑ n ∈ F, c n * Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (lam n : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) *
          e n (chart f p)‖ ^ 4)) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (C * (∑ n ∈ F, (1 + lam n) ^ s * ‖c n‖ ^ 2) ^ 2)

/-- `s* < 1/4`: the `L⁴` Strichartz estimate on the cube surface holds with a loss of fewer than
`1/4` derivatives. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  (∃ (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ), IsEigenbasis lam e) ∧
    ∃ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s ∧ s < 1 / 4 ∧
      ∀ (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ), IsEigenbasis lam e → ∃ C : ℝ, StrichartzL4 lam e s C

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM089
M_fix_reason: Well posed. For the board, the primary target is s* < 1/4 (the open improvement), with the conjecture s* = 0 noted.
prov_reason: Specializes Blair–Ford–Marzuola's Strichartz estimates on flat cone surfaces to the cube surface, where they suggest the 1/p loss is an artefact; asks for the sharp loss there.

title: Does an oscillating source lower the Strauss exponent?
results: Bound p_c<=1+sqrt2 is correct: John/Zhou iteration uses only |F(u)|<=C|u|^p and |F(u)-F(v)|<=C(|u|+|v|)^{p-1}|u-v|, both hold for g(t)|u|^p. The 'resonance predicts 2' heuristic (exp of int t^{1-p}) is arithmetically right but not an argument; a normal-form attempt (H''=g) just recycles the oscillating factor, so nothing is proved.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.28389 (2026 preprint): cited background on Strauss-type problems with time-dependent coefficients; the statement does not depend on it.
plain: For the 3D wave equation with source |u|^p, small smooth data give global solutions exactly when p > 1+√2 (Strauss). Multiply the source by a factor that oscillates periodically in time with average zero, such as cos t. The global-existence proof still works above 1+√2. Every blow-up proof below it breaks, because they all need the source to be positive. Is the true threshold strictly smaller?
math: For u_tt − Δu = cos(t)|u|^p on R^{1+3} (continuous Kirchhoff–Duhamel mild solutions), is p_c < 1+√2, i.e. does some p in (1,1+√2) have small-data global existence for all real C_c^∞ data? Exact p_c, dependence on g and lifespan are not formalized; the all-g version is ClaimGeneral (secondary).
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M090: Does an oscillating source lower the Strauss exponent?
For the 3D wave equation with source |u|^p, small smooth data give global solutions exactly when
p > 1+√2 (Strauss). Multiply the source by a factor that oscillates periodically in time with
average zero, such as cos t. The global-existence proof still works above 1+√2. Every blow-up
proof below it breaks, because they all need the source to be positive. Is the true threshold
strictly smaller?
Informal statement: For u_tt − Δu = cos(t)|u|^p on ℝ^{1+3} with data ε(f,h), f,h ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ³;ℝ),
let p_c = inf{p > 1 : ∀ f,h ∃ ε₀ > 0 such that the solution is global for all 0 < ε < ε₀}
(p_c ≤ 1+√2 by the John/Zhou/Glassey argument). Is p_c < 1+√2? (`Claim`: yes, for the model
g = cos t. The general mean-zero periodic g, the exact value of p_c (heuristically 2) and the
lifespan asymptotics are not part of `Claim`; `ClaimGeneral` below is the all-g version.)
Formalization notes:
* Solution class: continuous mild solutions defined by the Kirchhoff–Duhamel formula, the class
  in which John's and Glassey's theorems are proved in 3D:
    u(x,t) = ε·[∂ₜ(t M_f(x,t)) + t M_h(x,t)] + ∫₀ᵗ (t−s) M_{F(s)}(x, t−s) ds,
  F(s)(y) = g(s)|u(y,s)|^p, with M_φ(x,r) = (1/4π)∫_{S²} φ(x + rω) dω the spherical mean
  (written in spherical coordinates θ ∈ [0,π], ϕ ∈ [0,2π] with weight sin θ). The first bracket
  is the free wave with data (εf, εh) (Kirchhoff). u is required continuous on ℝ³ × [0,∞), so
  every integrand is continuous on a compact domain and no Bochner-integral junk value arises.
* For p > 1 the nonlinearity is locally Lipschitz, and the Kirchhoff kernel is positive and
  bounded on backward cones, so continuous mild solutions are unique (Gronwall); hence "the
  solution is global" ⇔ "a continuous mild solution exists on all of [0,∞)". For C² data/
  solutions this class coincides with classical solutions; for 1 < p < 2 (where |u|^p is not C²)
  it is the standard weak notion. John's theorem (p > 1+√2 small-data global existence) and,
  for g ≡ 1, blow-up for p < 1+√2 both hold in this class, so the class is non-degenerate.
* p_c < 1+√2 ⇔ some p ∈ (1, 1+√2) has the small-data global existence property (definition of
  infimum), which is how `Claim` is written; no sInf junk is involved. Note the property is
  required for every pair of real C_c^∞ data (f,h), as in the definition of p_c.
* Proving `Claim` = an oscillating source lowers the critical exponent. Proving `¬Claim` = for
  every p ∈ (1, 1+√2) some data blow up for arbitrarily small ε, i.e. the Strauss exponent is
  robust for g = cos t.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM090
noncomputable section

/-- Points of ℝ³. -/
abbrev R3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- Unit vector with spherical coordinates `(θ, ϕ)`. -/
def sph (θ ϕ : ℝ) : R3 := ![Real.sin θ * Real.cos ϕ, Real.sin θ * Real.sin ϕ, Real.cos θ]

/-- Spherical mean `M_φ(x, r) = (1/4π) ∫_{S²} φ(x + r ω) dω`. -/
def sphereMean (φ : R3 → ℝ) (x : R3) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (4 * Real.pi)) *
    ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi, ∫ ϕ in (0 : ℝ)..(2 * Real.pi), φ (x + r • sph θ ϕ) * Real.sin θ

/-- Kirchhoff solution of the free wave equation with data `(f, h)`. -/
def freeWave (f h : R3 → ℝ) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  deriv (fun τ : ℝ => τ * sphereMean f x τ) t + t * sphereMean h x t

/-- `u` is a global continuous mild solution of `u_tt − Δu = g(t)|u|^p` with data `ε(f,h)`. -/
def IsGlobalMild (g : ℝ → ℝ) (p ε : ℝ) (f h : R3 → ℝ) (u : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn (fun z : R3 × ℝ => u z.1 z.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) ∧
  ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t →
    u x t = ε * freeWave f h x t +
      ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..t, (t - s) * sphereMean (fun y : R3 => g s * |u y s| ^ p) x (t - s)

/-- Small-data global existence for every pair of smooth compactly supported data. -/
def SmallDataGlobal (g : ℝ → ℝ) (p : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f h : R3 → ℝ, (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k f) → HasCompactSupport f →
    (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k h) → HasCompactSupport h →
    ∃ ε₀ : ℝ, 0 < ε₀ ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < ε₀ → ∃ u : R3 → ℝ → ℝ, IsGlobalMild g p ε f h u

/-- For `g = cos t` the critical exponent is strictly below the Strauss exponent `1 + √2`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℝ, 1 < p ∧ p < 1 + Real.sqrt 2 ∧ SmallDataGlobal Real.cos p

/-- Admissible oscillating coefficients: smooth, `2π`-periodic, mean zero, not identically 0. -/
def Admissible (g : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k g) ∧ Function.Periodic g (2 * Real.pi) ∧
    (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..(2 * Real.pi), g t) = 0 ∧ ∃ t : ℝ, g t ≠ 0

/-- Secondary (not part of `Claim`): the same for every admissible `g`. -/
def ClaimGeneral : Prop :=
  ∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, Admissible g → ∃ p : ℝ, 1 < p ∧ p < 1 + Real.sqrt 2 ∧ SmallDataGlobal g p

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM090
prov_reason: Reviewer searches found no prior work on mean-zero time-oscillating sources for the Strauss problem; the question is QED's.

On $\mathbb T^3$ let $\omega:\mathbb T^3	imes[0,T)	o\mathbb R^3$ solve $\partial_t\omega+(u\cdot
abla)\omega=-S\omega$, where $u=
abla	imes(-\Delta)^{-1}(\omega-\langle\omegaangle)$, $S=	frac12(
abla u+

abla\cdot\omega_0=0$ generates a global smooth solution.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M091: Euler with reversed stretching
Flip the sign of the vortex-stretching term in the 3D Euler vorticity equation on the torus, keeping advection and the
Biot–Savart law. Do smooth solutions stay smooth forever, or can they blow up in finite time?
Informal statement: On 𝕋³ let ω : 𝕋³ × [0,T) → ℝ³ solve ∂ₜω + (u·∇)ω = −Sω, where u = ∇ × (−Δ)⁻¹(ω − ⟨ω⟩),
S = ½(∇u + ∇uᵀ) and ⟨ω⟩ is the spatial mean. Decide whether every ω₀ ∈ C^∞(𝕋³; ℝ³) with ∇·ω₀ = 0 generates a global
smooth solution.
Formalization notes: 𝕋³ = (ℝ/2πℤ)³ is encoded by 2π-periodic functions on ℝ³ = (Fin 3 → ℝ). Spatial partial derivatives
are Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions (`pd i F x = ∂ᵢF(x)`), the time derivative is `deriv`. The spatial mean is
(2π)⁻³ times the Bochner integral over the cell [0,2π]³. The Biot–Savart velocity is u = curl ψ where ψ is the
mean-zero periodic solution of Δψ = −(ω − ⟨ω⟩) (unique; ψ is required to exist as part of the solution, and its
joint smoothness is automatic for smooth ω, so requiring it loses nothing). We do NOT assume div ω = 0 for t > 0
(the reversed equation does not preserve it), which is why u is defined through ψ rather than by curl u = ω.
(Sω)ᵢ = Σⱼ ½(∂ⱼuᵢ + ∂ᵢuⱼ)ωⱼ. Smoothness is "C^k for every k ∈ ℕ" jointly in (t,x) on ℝ × ℝ³; since any smooth function on
[0,∞) × ℝ³ extends smoothly to t < 0, this is the same as smoothness on [0,∞) × 𝕋³. The equation is imposed for t > 0
(it then holds at t = 0 by continuity). Smooth solutions are unique, so existence of a global smooth solution is
the same as absence of finite-time blow-up. Proving Claim = global regularity for all smooth divergence-free data;
proving ¬Claim = some smooth periodic divergence-free ω₀ with no global smooth solution (finite-time blow-up).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM091

/-- Partial derivative `∂ᵢ F (x)` of a vector field `F : ℝ³ → ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def pd (i : Fin 3) (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ F x (Pi.single i 1)

/-- Vector Laplacian. -/
noncomputable def lap (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, pd i (pd i F) x

/-- Curl `∇ × F`. -/
noncomputable def curl (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ :=
  ![pd 1 F x 2 - pd 2 F x 1, pd 2 F x 0 - pd 0 F x 2, pd 0 F x 1 - pd 1 F x 0]

/-- Divergence `∇ · F`. -/
noncomputable def divg (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, pd i F x i

/-- `F` is `2π`-periodic in each coordinate (a field on `𝕋³`). -/
def IsPeriodic (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) (i : Fin 3), F (x + Pi.single i (2 * Real.pi)) = F x

/-- The fundamental cell `[0, 2π]³`. -/
noncomputable def cell : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ) := Set.Icc (0 : Fin 3 → ℝ) (fun _ => 2 * Real.pi)

/-- Spatial mean over the torus. -/
noncomputable def mean (F : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Fin 3 → ℝ :=
  (1 / (2 * Real.pi) ^ 3) • MeasureTheory.integral (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict cell) F

/-- `(S ω)ᵢ = Σⱼ ½ (∂ⱼ uᵢ + ∂ᵢ uⱼ) ωⱼ` with `S` the symmetric gradient of `u` at `x`. -/
noncomputable def strainApply (u : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (w : Fin 3 → ℝ) (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ :=
  fun i => ∑ j : Fin 3, (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (pd j u x i + pd i u x j) * w j

/-- Joint smoothness in `(t, x)`: `C^k` for every `k`. -/
def IsSmoothTX (f : ℝ → (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k (fun p : ℝ × (Fin 3 → ℝ) => f p.1 p.2)

/-- `(ω, ψ)` is a global smooth solution with initial vorticity `ω₀`; the velocity is `u(t) = curl ψ(t)`. -/
def IsGlobalSolution (ω₀ : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (ω ψ : ℝ → (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  IsSmoothTX ω ∧ IsSmoothTX ψ ∧ ω 0 = ω₀ ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
    IsPeriodic (ω t) ∧ IsPeriodic (ψ t) ∧ mean (ψ t) = 0 ∧
    ∀ x : Fin 3 → ℝ, lap (ψ t) x = -(ω t x - mean (ω t))) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ x : Fin 3 → ℝ,
    deriv (fun s : ℝ => ω s x) t + ∑ j : Fin 3, (curl (ψ t) x j) • pd j (ω t) x
      = -(strainApply (curl (ψ t)) (ω t x) x))

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ω₀ : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ),
    (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k ω₀) → IsPeriodic ω₀ → (∀ x, divg ω₀ x = 0) →
      ∃ ω ψ : ℝ → (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ), IsGlobalSolution ω₀ ω ψ

end OpenProblems.QEDM091
prov_reason: No source poses the 3D Euler model with reversed vortex stretching; only 1D analogues (De Gregorio, Córdoba–Córdoba–Fontelos, Okamoto–Sakajo–Wunsch, Elgindi–Jeong) study the sign of stretching.

title: Forced blow-up up to the Lions threshold
credit: OpenAI, forced Navier–Stokes blow-up (Sep 2026, unrefereed PDF); Lions (1969) for α ≥ 5/4; Tao, averaged Navier–Stokes (arXiv:1402.0290).

plain: With an ordinary Laplacian, a smooth compactly supported push can make a fluid at rest blow up in finite time (OpenAI, 2026). With dissipation (-Δ)^α for α ≥ 5/4, Lions proved that solutions stay smooth. Does forced blow-up from rest still happen for every α strictly between 1 and 5/4?

For $\alpha\in(1,5/4)$ consider $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u+
abla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$, $
abla\cdot u=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$, $u(\cdot,0)=0$. Determine the set of $\alpha\in(1,5/4)$ for which there exists $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3	imes(0,\infty);\mathbb R^3)$ whose unique smooth solution satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow T}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$ for some $T<\infty$. In particular, is it all of $(1,5/4)$, or is it nonempty?
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M092: Forced blow-up up to the Lions threshold
With an ordinary Laplacian, a smooth compactly supported push can make a fluid at rest blow up in
finite time (OpenAI, 2026). With dissipation (−Δ)^α for α ≥ 5/4, Lions proved that solutions stay
smooth. Does forced blow-up from rest still happen for every α strictly between 1 and 5/4?
Informal statement: For α ∈ (1,5/4) consider ∂ₜu + (u·∇)u + ∇p = −(−Δ)^α u + f, ∇·u = 0 on ℝ³,
u(·,0) = 0. Determine the set of α ∈ (1,5/4) for which there is f ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ³ × (0,∞); ℝ³) whose
unique smooth solution satisfies limsup_{t↑T} ‖u(t)‖_{L^∞} = ∞ for some T < ∞. `Claim` is the
board's precise target: this set is all of (1,5/4). (Nonemptiness is the weaker milestone
`ClaimSome`.)
Formalization notes:
* Space is `Fin 3 → ℝ`; derivatives are Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions, so the
  (sup) norm Mathlib puts on `Fin 3 → ℝ` never matters; Euclidean length is written out (`eucl`,
  `sqNorm`). Lebesgue measure is `volume` on `Fin 3 → ℝ`.
* Fractional Laplacian. Write α = 1 + s with s ∈ (0, 1/4). On H^∞ fields (−Δ)^α = (−Δ)^s(−Δ),
  so −(−Δ)^α u = (−Δ)^s(Δu), and for 0 < s < 1/2 the operator (−Δ)^s on bounded C¹ functions
  with bounded gradient is the absolutely convergent singular integral
    (−Δ)^s ψ(x) = C(3,s) ∫ (ψ(x) − ψ(x+y)) / |y|^{3+2s} dy,
    C(3,s) = 4^s Γ(3/2 + s) / (π^{3/2} |Γ(−s)|),
  which equals the Fourier multiplier |ξ|^{2s} (Di Nezza–Palatucci–Valdinoci, Prop. 3.3). We
  require the integrand to be Lebesgue integrable at every (x,t) used, so no Bochner junk value
  can enter the equation; the true solution (u(t) ∈ H^∞) satisfies this.
* Solution class (making "the unique smooth solution blows up at T" precise, cf. QED-M093):
  u, p are restrictions of functions that are C^k for all k on ℝ³ × (−∞,T) (values for t < 0 are
  irrelevant); the equations hold for 0 < t < T; u(·,0) = 0; uniformly bounded energy
  sup_{t<T} ∫|u|² < ∞; for each t < T the pressure is bounded (rules out harmonic, e.g. linear,
  pressures acting as a hidden force); u is bounded on ℝ³ × [0,T'] for every T' < T (rules out
  Tychonoff-type solutions with spatial growth or sup-norm infinite at fixed times, so that
  unboundedness can only come from t ↑ T); and u is unbounded on ℝ³ × [0,T). In this class
  (L^∞_t L²_x ∩ L^∞_t L^∞_x on each [0,T']) smooth solutions are unique by weak–strong uniqueness,
  so such a (u,p) is the unique smooth solution and limsup_{t↑T} ‖u(t)‖_∞ = ∞.
* The force f is C^k for all k on ℝ³ × ℝ and vanishes outside {|xᵢ| ≤ R, δ ≤ t ≤ R}, δ > 0
  (compact support in ℝ³ × (0,∞)).
* Proving `Claim` = forced blow-up from rest for every α ∈ (1,5/4). Proving `¬Claim` = some
  α ∈ (1,5/4) admits no such blow-up (global regularity from rest for all C_c^∞ forces).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM092
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory

/-- Points of ℝ³. -/
abbrev R3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- Squared Euclidean length. -/
def sqNorm (v : R3) : ℝ := ∑ i : Fin 3, v i ^ 2

/-- Euclidean length. -/
def eucl (v : R3) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (sqNorm v)

/-- Standard basis vector `eᵢ`. -/
def basisVec (i : Fin 3) : R3 := Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)

/-- Spatial partial derivative `∂ᵢ u (x,t)`. -/
def dx (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (i : Fin 3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => u y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Spatial Laplacian. -/
def lap (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx (fun y s => dx u i y s) i x t

/-- Time derivative. -/
def dt (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  deriv (fun s : ℝ => u x s) t

/-- Convective term `(u·∇)u`. -/
def convec (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ j : Fin 3, (u x t j) • dx u j x t

/-- Spatial gradient of a scalar field. -/
def grad (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fun i => fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => p y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Divergence. -/
def divg (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx u i x t i

/-- Normalising constant `C(3,s) = 4^s Γ(3/2+s) / (π^{3/2} |Γ(−s)|)`. -/
def fracConst (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (4 : ℝ) ^ s * Real.Gamma (3 / 2 + s) / (Real.pi ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) * |Real.Gamma (-s)|)

/-- Integrand of the singular-integral form of `(−Δ)^s ψ (x)`. -/
def kernelIntegrand (s : ℝ) (ψ : R3 → R3) (x y : R3) : R3 :=
  (eucl y ^ (3 + 2 * s))⁻¹ • (ψ x - ψ (x + y))

/-- `(−Δ)^s ψ (x)` for `0 < s < 1/2`. -/
def fracLap (s : ℝ) (ψ : R3 → R3) (x : R3) : R3 :=
  fracConst s • ∫ y : R3, kernelIntegrand s ψ x y

/-- `(f,u,p,T)`: forced hyperdissipative Navier–Stokes from rest, smooth on `[0,T)`, blowing up
in `L^∞` as `t ↑ T`; dissipation `(−Δ)^α`, written as `−(−Δ)^α u = (−Δ)^{α−1}(Δu)`. -/
def ForcedBlowup (α T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < T ∧
  -- smooth force with compact support in ℝ³ × (0, ∞)
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => f q.1 q.2)) ∧
  (∃ R δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), f x t ≠ 0 →
      (δ ≤ t ∧ t ≤ R ∧ ∀ i : Fin 3, |x i| ≤ R)) ∧
  -- smoothness of u and p up to (but excluding) time T
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => u q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => p q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  -- the fractional dissipation is given by an absolutely convergent integral
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      Integrable (fun y : R3 => kernelIntegrand (α - 1) (fun z : R3 => lap u z t) x y)) ∧
  -- the equations on ℝ³ × (0,T)
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t < T →
      dt u x t + convec u x t + grad p x t
        = fracLap (α - 1) (fun z : R3 => lap u z t) x + f x t) ∧
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t < T → divg u x t = 0) ∧
  -- start from rest
  (∀ x : R3, u x 0 = 0) ∧
  -- uniformly bounded energy
  (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      Integrable (fun x : R3 => sqNorm (u x t)) ∧ ∫ x : R3, sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C) ∧
  -- bounded pressure at each time
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : R3, |p x t| ≤ C) ∧
  -- bounded on ℝ³ × [0,T'] for every T' < T
  (∀ T' : ℝ, T' < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ T' → sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C) ∧
  -- but unbounded on ℝ³ × [0,T)
  (∀ M : ℝ, ∃ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t ∧ t < T ∧ M < sqNorm (u x t))

/-- For every `α ∈ (1, 5/4)` some smooth compactly supported force blows the fluid up from rest. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ α : ℝ, 1 < α → α < 5 / 4 →
    ∃ (T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ), ForcedBlowup α T f u p

/-- Weaker milestone (not part of `Claim`): the set of such `α` is nonempty. -/
def ClaimSome : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 1 < α ∧ α < 5 / 4 ∧
    ∃ (T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ), ForcedBlowup α T f u p

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM092
M_fix_reason: Well posed. For the board, the precise target is 'for every α ∈ (1,5/4) such f exists' (Claim), with 'nonempty' as the weaker milestone.
prov_reason: Extends the 2026 forced finite-time blow-up construction for the Laplacian (α = 1) to hyperdissipative α ∈ (1,5/4), up to Lions' regularity threshold; Tao and Coiculescu treat only averaged models.

title: Forced Navier–Stokes blow-up at a no-slip wall
credit: Extends the OpenAI 2026 forced Navier–Stokes blow-up (cdn.openai.com navier-stokes.pdf) and Cao–Chi–Nie, arXiv:2609.10262.

Inside a domain this can simply be copied away from any wall. Show that blow-up can also happen at the wall itself: in a half-space with the no-slip condition, the velocity becomes unbounded at a point of the boundary.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M093: Forced Navier–Stokes blow-up at a no-slip wall
In 2026 it was shown that a smooth, compactly supported force can drive the 3D Navier–Stokes
equations, started from rest, to blow up in finite time, but the construction is interior.
Show that blow-up can happen at the wall itself: in the half-space {x₃ > 0} with the no-slip
condition, a smooth finite-energy solution started from rest and driven by a smooth compactly
supported force becomes unbounded in finite time, while staying bounded away from the wall.
Informal statement: Let ℝ³₊ = {x₃ > 0}, ν > 0. Construct f ∈ C_c^∞(closure(ℝ³₊) × (0,∞); ℝ³) and a
solution (u,p) of ∂ₜu − νΔu + (u·∇)u + ∇p = f, ∇·u = 0 in ℝ³₊ × (0,T), u = 0 on {x₃ = 0},
u(·,0) = 0, with u ∈ C^∞(closure(ℝ³₊) × [0,T)), sup_{t<T} ‖u(t)‖_{L²} < ∞ and
limsup_{t↑T} ‖u(t)‖_{L^∞} = ∞, such that u stays bounded on {x₃ > r} × [0,T) for every r > 0
(all singular points lie on the wall).
Formalization notes: Space is `Fin 3 → ℝ`; coordinate `x 2` is the wall-normal x₃. Derivatives
are Fréchet derivatives (`fderiv`, `deriv`), so the norm on `Fin 3 → ℝ` is irrelevant; the
squared Euclidean length is written out as `sqNorm`. Smoothness up to the boundary on
closure(ℝ³₊) × [0,T) is encoded as: u and p are restrictions of functions that are C^k for every
k on the open set ℝ³ × (−∞,T) (equivalent by Seeley/Whitney extension); values with x₃ < 0 or
t < 0 are irrelevant. The force is C^k for all k on ℝ³ × ℝ and vanishes outside a box
{|xᵢ| ≤ R, δ ≤ t ≤ R} with δ > 0 (compact support in closure(ℝ³₊) × (0,∞)). Two side conditions
make "the singular points lie on (a bounded part of) the wall" precise and rule out cheap
solutions: (i) u is bounded on {x₃ ≥ 0, max(|x₁|,|x₂|) > R₀} × [0,T) (no escape to horizontal
infinity), and (ii) for each t < T the pressure p(·,t) is bounded on the closed half-space (this
excludes harmonic, e.g. linear, pressures acting as a hidden non-decaying force). Together with
boundedness on {x₃ > r} and smoothness on [0,T), unboundedness can only come from points of a
compact piece of the wall as t ↑ T. The energy condition requires x ↦ |u(x,t)|² integrable on
ℝ³₊ with uniformly bounded integral. Proving `Claim` = constructing such a blow-up for every
ν > 0; proving `¬Claim` = showing that for some ν > 0 no such boundary blow-up exists.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM093

open MeasureTheory

/-- Points of ℝ³; the coordinate `x 2` is the wall-normal coordinate x₃. -/
abbrev R3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- Squared Euclidean length of a vector in ℝ³. -/
def sqNorm (v : R3) : ℝ := ∑ i : Fin 3, v i ^ 2

/-- Standard basis vector `eᵢ`. -/
def basisVec (i : Fin 3) : R3 := Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)

/-- Spatial partial derivative `∂ᵢ u (x,t)` of a time-dependent vector field. -/
noncomputable def dx (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (i : Fin 3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => u y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Spatial Laplacian `Δu (x,t) = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ∂ᵢ u`. -/
noncomputable def lap (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx (fun y s => dx u i y s) i x t

/-- Time derivative `∂ₜ u (x,t)`. -/
noncomputable def dt (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  deriv (fun s : ℝ => u x s) t

/-- Convective term `(u·∇)u (x,t) = ∑ⱼ uⱼ ∂ⱼ u`. -/
noncomputable def convec (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ j : Fin 3, (u x t j) • dx u j x t

/-- Spatial gradient of a scalar field. -/
noncomputable def grad (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fun i => fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => p y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Divergence `∇·u (x,t)`. -/
noncomputable def divg (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx u i x t i

/-- The open half-space `{x₃ > 0}`. -/
def halfSpace : Set R3 := {x : R3 | 0 < x 2}

/-- `(f,u,p,T)` is a boundary blow-up solution of forced Navier–Stokes with viscosity `ν`
in the half-space with no-slip condition, as described in the header. -/
def BoundaryBlowup (ν T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < T ∧
  -- smooth force with compact support in closure(ℝ³₊) × (0, ∞)
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => f q.1 q.2)) ∧
  (∃ R δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), f x t ≠ 0 →
      (δ ≤ t ∧ t ≤ R ∧ ∀ i : Fin 3, |x i| ≤ R)) ∧
  -- smoothness of u and p up to the wall and up to (but excluding) time T
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => u q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => p q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  -- the equations in ℝ³₊ × (0,T)
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < x 2 → 0 < t → t < T →
      dt u x t - ν • lap u x t + convec u x t + grad p x t = f x t) ∧
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < x 2 → 0 < t → t < T → divg u x t = 0) ∧
  -- no-slip and initial condition
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), x 2 = 0 → 0 ≤ t → t < T → u x t = 0) ∧
  (∀ x : R3, 0 ≤ x 2 → u x 0 = 0) ∧
  -- finite energy, uniformly in time
  (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      IntegrableOn (fun x : R3 => sqNorm (u x t)) halfSpace ∧
      ∫ x in halfSpace, sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C) ∧
  -- pressure bounded at each time (excludes harmonic pressures)
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : R3, 0 ≤ x 2 → |p x t| ≤ C) ∧
  -- blow-up: u is unbounded on closure(ℝ³₊) × [0,T)
  (∀ M : ℝ, ∃ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ x 2 ∧ 0 ≤ t ∧ t < T ∧ M < sqNorm (u x t)) ∧
  -- bounded away from the wall
  (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), r < x 2 → 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C) ∧
  -- bounded far out along the wall (singularities in a compact part of the wall)
  (∃ R₀ C : ℝ, ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ x 2 → 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      (R₀ < |x 0| ∨ R₀ < |x 1|) → sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C)

/-- For every viscosity there is a forced boundary blow-up at a no-slip wall. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ν : ℝ, 0 < ν →
    ∃ (T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ), BoundaryBlowup ν T f u p

end OpenProblems.QEDM093
M_fix_reason: M is fine as a mathematical statement; the Lean adds two standard side conditions (bounded pressure at each time; u bounded far out along the wall) to pin down 'singular points on the wall' and exclude harmonic-pressure / spatial-infinity loopholes.
prov_reason: Boundary (no-slip wall) version of the 2026 interior forced blow-up construction; refs/notes find no half-space or boundary-singularity result.

title: Heat with a cosine reaction
credit: H. Fujita 1966 (critical exponent); R. Pinsky 1997 (weighted Fujita problem, a >= 0)
plain: In u_t = u_xx + cos(x) u^2 the reaction term averages to zero over a period, but a second-order (homogenization) effect produces an effective +u^3 term, which in one dimension is exactly Fujita's borderline exponent where every positive solution of u_t = u_xx + u^3 blows up. Does every positive solution of the cosine equation blow up in finite time?
math: Let $d\ge1$, $a\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ be $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic with $\int_{[0,1]^d}a=0$, $a\not\equiv0$. Consider $u_t=\Delta u+a(x)u^p$, $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R^d)$, $u_0\ge0$, $u_0\not\equiv0$. Prove: (i) if $1<p\le1+1/d$, every such solution blows up in finite time; (ii) if $p>1+1/d$, solutions with sufficiently small $u_0$ are global. Test case: $d=1$, $p=2$, $a=\cos(2\pi x)$ (equivalently $a=\cos x$ with $2\pi$-periodicity).
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-M094: Heat with a cosine reaction
For u_t = Δu + a(x)u^p with a periodic, mean-zero, not identically zero weight, the first-order reaction
averages out, but homogenization produces an effective +c·u^{2p−1} term, predicting the Fujita-type
threshold p* = 1 + 1/d. The test case u_t = u_xx + cos(2πx)u² is exactly critical.
Informal statement: Let d ≥ 1, a ∈ C^∞(ℝ^d) ℤ^d-periodic with ∫_{[0,1]^d} a = 0, a ≢ 0. Consider
u_t = Δu + a(x)u^p, u(·,0) = u₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^d), u₀ ≥ 0, u₀ ≢ 0. Prove: (i) if 1 < p ≤ 1 + 1/d, every such
solution blows up in finite time; (ii) if p > 1 + 1/d, then for every such u₀ the solution with
initial data εu₀ is global for all sufficiently small ε > 0.
Formalization notes: A global solution is u : ℝ^d × ℝ → ℝ, C² on {t > 0}, continuous on {t ≥ 0},
nonnegative, bounded on every strip ℝ^d × [0,T], with u(x,0) = u₀(x) and u_t = Δu + a u^p pointwise
for t > 0 (partials via `fderiv`; `u^p` is `Real.rpow`, meaningful since u ≥ 0; nonnegativity holds for
the true solution by the comparison principle). By local well-posedness and uniqueness in the class
of solutions bounded on strips, "blows up in finite time" ⇔ "no global solution in this class".
For (ii), "sufficiently small u₀" is read profile-wise (data εu₀, ε small), the standard Fujita form.
Smoothness of a is `∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n a`.
Proving `Claim` = both (i) and (ii) for all d, a, p. Proving `¬Claim` = a counterexample to either:
a global positive solution for some p ≤ 1 + 1/d, or a supercritical p and profile u₀ for which
arbitrarily small multiples blow up.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM094

/-- ℝ^d. -/
abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) : Type := Fin d → ℝ

/-- Spatial Laplacian of `u` at `z = (x,t)`. -/
noncomputable def lap {d : ℕ} (u : Rd d × ℝ → ℝ) (z : Rd d × ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin d,
    fderiv ℝ (fun y : Rd d × ℝ => fderiv ℝ u y ((Pi.single i (1 : ℝ) : Rd d), (0 : ℝ))) z
      ((Pi.single i (1 : ℝ) : Rd d), (0 : ℝ))

/-- Time derivative of `u` at `z`. -/
noncomputable def dt {d : ℕ} (u : Rd d × ℝ → ℝ) (z : Rd d × ℝ) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ u z ((0 : Rd d), (1 : ℝ))

/-- Admissible weight: smooth, ℤ^d-periodic, mean zero, not identically zero. -/
def AdmissibleWeight (d : ℕ) (a : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n a) ∧
  (∀ (x : Rd d) (i : Fin d), a (x + Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)) = a x) ∧
  (∫ x in Set.Icc (0 : Rd d) 1, a x) = 0 ∧
  (∃ x, a x ≠ 0)

/-- Admissible initial datum: continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative, not identically zero. -/
def AdmissibleDatum (d : ℕ) (u₀ : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous u₀ ∧ HasCompactSupport u₀ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ u₀ x) ∧ (∃ x, u₀ x ≠ 0)

/-- `u` is a global (bounded on strips) classical nonnegative solution. -/
def IsGlobalSolution (d : ℕ) (a : Rd d → ℝ) (p : ℝ) (u₀ : Rd d → ℝ) (u : Rd d × ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 2 u {z | 0 < z.2} ∧
  ContinuousOn u {z | 0 ≤ z.2} ∧
  (∀ x, u (x, 0) = u₀ x) ∧
  (∀ z : Rd d × ℝ, 0 ≤ z.2 → 0 ≤ u z) ∧
  (∀ T : ℝ, ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ z : Rd d × ℝ, 0 ≤ z.2 → z.2 ≤ T → |u z| ≤ M) ∧
  (∀ z : Rd d × ℝ, 0 < z.2 → dt u z = lap u z + a z.1 * u z ^ p)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → ∀ a : Rd d → ℝ, AdmissibleWeight d a → ∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p →
    (p ≤ 1 + 1 / (d : ℝ) →
      ∀ u₀ : Rd d → ℝ, AdmissibleDatum d u₀ → ∀ u : Rd d × ℝ → ℝ, ¬ IsGlobalSolution d a p u₀ u) ∧
    (1 + 1 / (d : ℝ) < p →
      ∀ u₀ : Rd d → ℝ, AdmissibleDatum d u₀ → ∃ ε₀ : ℝ, 0 < ε₀ ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < ε₀ →
        ∃ u : Rd d × ℝ → ℝ, IsGlobalSolution d a p (fun x => ε * u₀ x) u)

end OpenProblems.QEDM094
prov_reason: This extends Fujita's blow-up/global threshold to sign-changing, mean-zero periodic weights; the known weighted results (Pinsky and others) assume a >= 0.

title: KdV with a cosine coefficient
plain: Put a cos x in front of the cubic term of the modified KdV equation on the circle. The energy and the mean are still conserved, but the L² norm is not, and the energy no longer has a definite sign. Can smooth solutions blow up in finite time?
math: Consider $u_t+u_{xxx}+(\cos(x)\,u^3)_x=0$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ with real $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$. It is Hamiltonian, $u_t=\partial_x\frac{\delta H}{\delta u}$ with $H=\int(\tfrac12u_x^2-\tfrac14\cos(x)u^4)$, and conserves $\int u$ and $H$. However, $\frac{d}{dt}\int u^2=\frac12\int\sin(x)u^4$. Decide whether every such $u_0$ yields a global smooth solution, or whether $\|u(t)\|_{H^1}\to\infty$ in finite time for some $u_0$.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M095: KdV with a cosine coefficient
Put a cos x in front of the cubic term of the modified KdV equation on the circle. The energy
and the mean are still conserved, but the L² norm is not, and the energy is indefinite. Can
smooth solutions blow up in finite time?
Informal statement: Consider u_t + u_xxx + (cos(x) u³)_x = 0 on 𝕋 = ℝ/2πℤ with real
u₀ ∈ C^∞(𝕋). It is Hamiltonian with H = ∫(½u_x² − ¼cos(x)u⁴), conserves ∫u and H, and
d/dt ∫u² = ½∫ sin(x) u⁴. Decide whether every such u₀ yields a global smooth solution, or
whether ‖u(t)‖_{H¹} → ∞ in finite time for some u₀.
Formalization notes:
* Functions on 𝕋 are 2π-periodic functions on ℝ. A global smooth solution is
  u : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ (time, space), C^n for every n ∈ ℕ (i.e. C^∞; written this way to avoid
  `⊤` meaning analytic), 2π-periodic in x, with u(0,x) = u₀(x) and the equation holding
  pointwise for all t ≥ 0. Requiring u to be smooth on all of ℝ × ℝ (with the equation only
  for t ≥ 0) loses nothing: a C^∞ function on [0,∞) × 𝕋 extends smoothly to t < 0.
* Derivatives are partial derivatives via `deriv` of sections; `iteratedDeriv 3` for u_xxx.
* Proving `Claim`: every smooth periodic u₀ has a global smooth solution (global regularity).
  Proving `¬Claim`: some smooth u₀ has no global smooth solution; by standard local
  well-posedness in H^s (s large) with the blow-up alternative and persistence of regularity,
  this is equivalent to finite-time blow-up of ‖u(t)‖_{H¹} (the H¹ norm controls all higher
  norms for this equation), matching the dichotomy in the informal statement.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM095

/-- `u` is a global (forward in time) smooth 2π-periodic solution of
`u_t + u_xxx + (cos x · u³)_x = 0` with initial data `u₀`. -/
def IsGlobalSmoothSolution (u₀ : ℝ → ℝ) (u : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n u) ∧
  (∀ t x : ℝ, u (t, x + 2 * Real.pi) = u (t, x)) ∧
  (∀ x : ℝ, u (0, x) = u₀ x) ∧
  ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x : ℝ,
    deriv (fun s : ℝ => u (s, x)) t
      + iteratedDeriv 3 (fun y : ℝ => u (t, y)) x
      + deriv (fun y : ℝ => Real.cos y * (u (t, y)) ^ 3) x = 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ u₀ : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n u₀) → Function.Periodic u₀ (2 * Real.pi) →
    ∃ u : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, IsGlobalSmoothSolution u₀ u

end OpenProblems.QEDM095
M_fix_reason: Conservation laws and the L² identity check out (d/dt∫u² = ½∫ sin x u⁴). Well posed; the dichotomy is exhaustive given local well-posedness with H¹ blow-up alternative.

title: Liouville theorem for Lane-Emden with a shifted nonlinearity
plain: Gidas-Spruck: -Delta u = u^p has no positive solution on R^n for subcritical p. Replace u^p by the value of u^p at a shifted point x+e. Is there still no positive solution, for every subcritical p?
math: Let $n\ge3$, $1<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}$, $e\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$. Prove or disprove: there is no positive $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)$ with $-\Delta u(x)=u(x+e)^p$ for all $x$. (For $1<p<\frac n{n-2}$ the standard Mitidieri–Pohozaev test-function argument applies, since the shift is negligible at large scales; the open range is $\frac n{n-2}\le p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}$. One may also ask whether positive solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2}{n-2}$.)

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M096: Liouville theorem for Lane-Emden with a shifted nonlinearity
Gidas-Spruck: -Δu = u^p has no positive entire solution on R^n for 1 < p < (n+2)/(n-2). If the
nonlinearity is evaluated at a shifted point, -Δu(x) = u(x+e)^p with e ≠ 0, is there still no
positive solution for every subcritical p?
Informal statement: Let n >= 3, 1 < p < (n+2)/(n-2), e ∈ R^n \ {0}. Prove or disprove: there is no
positive u ∈ C^2(R^n) with -Δu(x) = u(x+e)^p for all x.
Formalization notes: R^n is `Fin n → ℝ`; the Laplacian is defined from the second Fréchet
derivative as Σ_i D^2u(x)(e_i, e_i) with e_i = `Pi.single i 1` (independent of the norm used).
u(x+e)^p is the real power `Real.rpow` (u > 0, so no junk values). Claim asserts nonexistence for
all n >= 3, all subcritical p > 1 and all e ≠ 0 simultaneously; ¬Claim means a positive C^2
solution exists for some such (n, p, e). The range 1 < p < n/(n-2) is believed to follow from
the Mitidieri-Pohozaev test-function method; the open range is n/(n-2) <= p < (n+2)/(n-2). The
supercritical question p >= (n+2)/(n-2) is not part of Claim.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM096

/-- The Laplacian of `u : ℝ^n → ℝ` at `x`, via the second Fréchet derivative. -/
noncomputable def laplacian {n : ℕ} (u : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) x (Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)) (Pi.single i (1 : ℝ))

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p → p < ((n : ℝ) + 2) / ((n : ℝ) - 2) →
    ∀ e : Fin n → ℝ, e ≠ 0 →
      ¬ ∃ u : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 2 u ∧ (∀ x, 0 < u x) ∧
        ∀ x, -(laplacian u x) = (u (x + e)) ^ p

end OpenProblems.QEDM096
prov_reason: Notes report no literature on shifted-argument Lane-Emden equations after two searches; the question is a new nonlocal variant formulated by QED.

title: Mass-critical scattering on flat cones
credit: B. Dodson, global well-posedness and scattering for the defocusing L^2-critical NLS in d=2 (Duke Math. J. 2016)
results: Both trivial cases check out. For alpha=2pi/k, C_alpha=R^2/Z_k: the Friedrichs modes e^{ikmθ} with Bessel order k|m| match the Z_k-invariant plane functions, and Dodson applies for any mass, with mass scaled by k. For radial data the m=0 mode on the cone is the 2D radial Laplacian. The sign convention iu_t+Δu=+|u|^2u is defocusing.
plain: Dodson proved that the defocusing cubic Schrodinger equation in the plane scatters for every finite-mass initial state. Prove the same on every flat cone, a plane with a single conical singularity of total angle alpha. For alpha = 2pi/k it follows from Dodson by symmetry, and radial data are also easy. Every other angle, such as the surface of a cube corner (alpha = 3pi/2) or alpha > 2pi, is open.
math: For $\alpha>0$ let $\mathcal C_\alpha=(0,\infty)\times(\mathbb R/\alpha\mathbb Z)$ with metric $dr^2+r^2d\theta^2$ and $\Delta$ the Friedrichs extension of the Laplacian on $C_c^\infty(\mathcal C_\alpha)$. Prove that for every $\alpha>0$ and every $u_0\in L^2(\mathcal C_\alpha)$ the solution of $iu_t+\Delta u=|u|^2u$, $u(0)=u_0$, is global with $\|u\|_{L^4_{t,x}(\mathbb R\times\mathcal C_\alpha)}<\infty$, hence scatters in $L^2$. (Known: $\alpha=2\pi/k$, since $\mathcal C_{2\pi/k}=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z_k$ and Dodson applies to $\mathbb Z_k$-invariant data. Radial data for any $\alpha$, since the radial equation coincides with the 2D one.)
